Additionally, A child `ThreadGroup` must retain a `parent_thread_group` `shared_ptr` so the parent remains alive while child trackers point to it through raw pointers.

canonical_claim: Using early projection or sub-part commits to make staged files readable creates windows in which orphan temporary metadata or blobs can remain after an exception.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: An R5-round review found a CRITICAL trust-flip bug where finding #19's guard made `CasProbe` vacuous on Native S3 pools: wrong-dialect probe tokens were being rejected locally before ever going over the wire, at three call sites in `CasProbe.cpp:93,143,172`; the fix applies a live-dialect probe at all three sites plus a reachability test that pins non-vacuousness.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: A StorageProxy virtual-forwarding audit found roughly 60 unforwarded virtuals (about 45 that must be forwarded), including a CRITICAL silent-empty `backupData`; `mutate` forwarding was correct, rename forwarding moved to `StorageTableProxy`, and `detach` forwarding was dropped.

canonical_claim: Three distinct lazy-proxy bugs were found during this round: (1) `StorageProxy` forwarded `mutate` but not `checkMutationIsPossible`, so a lazy proxy rejected all mutations (`MATERIALIZE TTL` -> `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`); (2) the proxy's cached metadata lacked TTL info, breaking `MATERIALIZE TTL` a second way after the first fix; both were fixed and validated by the narrowed stateless test 05021.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The current fsck oracle assumes a snapshot ID is also a log ID and silently skips a recovery seal on that assumption, rather than reporting the skip as checked; and repeated per-held-namespace anchor/repair GETs on every folding round are rate-bounded only by the scheduler, with no cumulative bound or backoff.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: SEC-4: a pool-write-capable party (or a corrupt/huge object) can place a valid-CRC, valid-framing but enormous shard or manifest directly in S3; decoders (`decodeRootShard`, `decodePartManifest`) validate magic/version/CRC/journal-integrity but a valid giant body still allocates on decode, causing OOM in readers and the GC folder (GC folds whole journals). Recommendation: enforce absolute decode-side size/element caps independent of the write path, and stream large journals in the fold.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: SEC-5: key builders route through `checkNamespace`, `namespaceFileKey`, and `mountpointObjectKey`, which reject empty segments, the reserved `_files`/`_manifests`/`_precommits` names, `..`, leading/trailing `/`, and `//`, but `checkNamespace` itself does not reject a `..` segment; this is safe only because the backend is an object store with literal (non-normalized) keys, so a filesystem-backed or path-normalizing backend would be vulnerable to traversal. Recommendation: reject `..` in `checkNamespace` so the invariant does not silently depend on backend key semantics.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The CA transient-classifier audit flags two ErrorCode-consistency mistags on the Mount plane: `CasServerRoot.cpp:261`'s 100-attempt CAS loop is coded `CORRUPTED_DATA` while sibling sites use `ABORTED`, and `:241` bundles `ContainerAbsent`/`AccessDenied`/`Indeterminate` together as corruption; both are contained but inconsistent.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: D3 (mostly duplicated with meaningful differences): three separate conditional-write retry regimes exist for the same class of operation — `CasRequestController` (ref lane: single-attempt client, budget, fence-gated, resolve-before-reissue), plain-object `casPutObject`/`casRemoveObject` loops (`MAX_CAS_ATTEMPTS=100`, default retry policy), and `CasBuild`'s local loops (`max_attempts=8`) — and only the ref lane implements the lease-deadline model; the plain-object gap is a real hazard.

canonical_claim: D9: `ObjectStorageBackend` implements overlapping token-policy logic (native ETag vs emulated vs Generation) independently across `head`/`list`/`casPut`/`deleteExact`/`supportsListTokens`, corroborated by a past real incident (the `EmulatedSingleProcess` list-vs-head token mismatch); this is called out as the highest-value consolidation target in the report.

canonical_claim: Risk register #8 (Medium, confirmed): the destructive `GC REBUILD` verb (which overwrites `gc/state` and, when no disk is given, loops over ALL CA disks) shares one access right with the benign per-round `GC` verb (`AccessType.h:351`; `InterpreterSystemQuery.cpp:1004,1010`), so an operator cannot grant "run a round" without also granting disaster-recovery rebuild, and a broad accidental `SYSTEM ... GC REBUILD` rebuilds every pool. Suggested action: a dedicated access right; consider requiring an explicit disk for rebuild.

topic: CAS correctness

canonical_claim: CasRequestController::putIfAbsentControlled gates every attempt by the fence and remaining deadline, resolves uncertain writes by exact GET, and treats differing existing bytes as CORRUPTED_DATA.

canonical_claim: Build::promote validates the manifest, checks the precommit owner, revalidates required blob leaves, and publishes the precommit-to-committed binding only after those checks.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: GC must not delete an object while any session pin or committed reference names it, preserving `INV_NO_LOSS` and `INV_NO_DANGLE`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: Deterministic GC artifacts such as in-degree runs and fold seals must be byte-identical on collision, otherwise GC fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`. topic: CAS correctness

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: A retired entry whose in-degree recovers above zero is spared even when it is already `delete_pending`. Additionally, A pending delete is terminal: a pending entry with recovered in-degree is spared and logged loudly, while re-executing a pending delete is safe at any leader staleness; a failed CAS cannot publish a zombie leader's fresh decisions.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: If an exact delete reports `created_delete_marker = true`, GC throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` because versioning tombstones can violate `INV_NO_RETURN`.

topic: CAS correctness

Additionally, CAS failure handling is conservative: lost folds, stale snapshots, duplicated records, and crashed leaders can only postpone reclamation because in-degree is an idempotent set of source edges rather than a counter.

canonical_claim: A point-in-time `HEAD -> 404` is not durable absence; unreadable bodies clamp the fold and any clamped pass suppresses destructive decisions.

canonical_claim: Per-hash metadata is an advisory freshness point-read, not the blob lifetime linearization point; exactness remains with the in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body delete.

canonical_claim: CA tests are single-process, single-threaded, and clock-free for GC scenarios; genuine concurrency correctness rests on backend primitives, TLA+ models, and integration or soak tests rather than gtests alone.

canonical_claim: Only the adopted attempt's artifact may be consulted by GC decisions; a deposed leader's artifacts must remain reader-invisible.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The GC safety assertion is `{preview deletes} ⊆ {ca-fsck unreachable}`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: Positive scenarios assert that `system.content_addressed_log` contains no `read_missing`, `dangling_access`, `corrupt_dangle`, `corrupt_decode`, `snap_journal_incoherent`, or `exception` events.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: `readManifest` fails closed with `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST` and `INV-NO-DANGLE` when a live ref names a missing manifest.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: `readManifest` rejects a body whose self-described ref does not match the journal `ManifestRef` or whose `root_namespace_id` does not match the owning namespace with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: A live committed manifest ref structurally protects its referenced blobs from GC because the fold cannot mark them zero-in-degree, and deletion additionally waits through condemn and `delete_pending`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The current CAS safety model assumes one-live-object semantics; versioned-bucket marker stacks and version-specific conditional behavior are unmodeled.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The CAS safety triad is no-dangle, no-loss, and no-return: live references resolve through present keys, deletion requires durable retirement and later zero reachability with the exact token, and a retired `(kind, hash, token)` cannot become a valid dependency again.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: An operation with an uncertain conditional-write outcome is treated as `PrecommitState::Uncertain`, which behaves as `NotAttempted` for admission and as `Durable` for cleanup.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: `writer_epoch` is durable-monotone and never reissued, and every re-materialization of a fixed `(namespace, shard)` carries a strictly greater incarnation to close ABA. Additionally, `writer_epoch` is durably monotone, while `build_sequence` resets on process start; global ordering is the lexicographic pair `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)`. topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: CAS crash safety is intentionally asymmetric: every crash point may leak objects, but no crash point loses acknowledged data or creates a dangling reference.

topic: CAS correctness

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: D1 requires `THM-NO-RETURN`, `INV-NO-DANGLING`, `INV-NO-ABA`, and `INV-NO-BLOB-LEAK`; the last requires every `-1` edge to be folded before its carrying shard is deleted.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: Copy-forward verification requires a valid envelope, matching object kind, and recomputed logical hash equal to the key hash; any mismatch or 404 is fail-closed, with corruption reported as `CORRUPTED_DATA` and a lost-race 404 as `ABORTED`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: `CaGcAckFloorCore` models copy-forward as minting and binding a fresh incarnation only while the blob is present and the current token is visible in the writer's loaded retired view; there is no absent-source copy-forward arm.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The ack-floor redesign rejects old schema versions fail-closed: schema versions are bumped, malformed data yields `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and future versions yield `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: A GC pass must durably write retired-list and snapshot runs before the `gc/state` CAS that publishes `round := K`, so any reader observing round K can load retired-list version K.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: GC fence-outs complete before discovery and their writers' last commits are therefore durable before the sweep begins.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The heartbeat drain proves that a server advertising `observed_gc_round = A` has no in-flight commit using a view below A.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: If `snap_generation > 0` but the adopted fold seal, a referenced run, or a referenced retired object is absent or corrupt, GC must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` rather than treating the artifact as an empty baseline.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The rebuild is live-conservative: events after a shard read remain above the recorded cursor for the next regular round, a live precommit with an absent body clamps the cursor below its transition, and new condemnations wait for mount acknowledgements past the rebuilt round.

topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: The GCS dialect throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` for an `If-None-Match` value other than `*` and for a non-numeric `If-Match` value, rather than silently changing conditional semantics. topic: CAS correctness
canonical_claim: Before applying each queued closure, the leader snapshots the in-memory `RootShard`; if the closure throws, the snapshot is restored, that promise receives the exception, and the remaining batch items continue.

topic: CAS correctness

topic: Snapshot coverage and GC fold coverage

topic: Snapshot and log bodies are deterministic
canonical_claim: Snapshot and log bodies are deterministic and repeat key-derived identity fields; a snapshot is never renamed or copied when created, and logs remain under their original keys.

topic: Snapshot rows are sorted by canonical

topic: State-growing operations are admitted only if
canonical_claim: State-growing operations are admitted only if both the encoded snapshot and encoded namespace-removal transaction remain below their respective hard budgets; an oversized operation fails closed before object creation.

topic: Replacing an existing committed ref requires
canonical_claim: Replacing an existing committed ref requires an explicit `owner_transition` removal before promotion; silent displacement is forbidden because GC derives edges from explicit operations rather than state diffs.

topic: If a selected snapshot or tail
canonical_claim: If a selected snapshot or tail body disappears between recovery `LIST` and `GET`, the writer restarts with a fresh `LIST`; absence is not corruption and recovery never falls back to an older plausible snapshot.

topic: An uncertain ref-log create is never
canonical_claim: An uncertain ref-log create is never treated as failed when an exact-key GET finds absence; the append lane remains wedged until identical bytes are observed, a whitelisted definite rejection is proven, or the writer unmounts.

topic: A `PreconditionFailed` ref-log create always resolves
canonical_claim: A `PreconditionFailed` ref-log create always resolves through exact-key observation: identical bytes mean success of the earlier attempt, while different bytes are corruption. topic: The snapshot published by the writer
canonical_claim: The snapshot published by the writer is an integrity oracle: fsck can replay the snapshot and tail and compare the deterministic bytes, with divergence treated as corruption.

topic: GC resumes pagination exactly after the
canonical_claim: GC resumes pagination exactly after the last key returned by the previous page; opaque continuation tokens are usable only when the backend documents equivalent positioning semantics.

topic: A ref fold aborts without partial

topic: Namespace cleanup deletes only exact keys
canonical_claim: Namespace cleanup deletes only exact keys captured by its own enumeration and never uses a prefix wildcard; after recreation, exact keys from the removed incarnation cannot name newly created objects.

topic: If the existing destination is condemned

topic: Recovery must not promote a precommit

canonical_claim: The two-leader regression must verify that after a spare the marker remains `Condemned`, a writer resurrects to a fresh token `t2`, and stale `deleteExact(t1)` returns `TokenMismatch` or `Replaced` without removing the live body.

topic: The reader recovery invariant is `Replay(newest
canonical_claim: The reader recovery invariant is `Replay(newest visible valid snapshot, surviving later logs) = Replay(full history)` for every reader that completes, including readers that restart.

topic: Cleanup must not remove an object
canonical_claim: Cleanup must not remove an object still needed by a completing reader, and namespace recreation must not observe a stale delete.

topic: Ref state rejects birth on a

topic: The replay equation requires replaying a

canonical_claim: Five gap tests closed the audit's unit-testable fail-closed gaps: the CAS GC baseline guard, one-operation-per-ref batch cut, mountpoint get/remove round trip, unknown owner-kind rejection, and invalid ref-log-body fold abort.

topic: The audit found no remaining fail-closed
canonical_claim: The audit found no remaining fail-closed branch that was both unit-testable and unjustified after the gap tests and integration/soak dispositions.

topic: CAS correctness requires distinguishing definitely committed

topic: An uncertain tokened conditional overwrite cannot

topic: After an uncertain immutable conditional create

topic: Part-manifest encode and decode enforce canonical

canonical_claim: The retry-later API has both `throwCasWriteRetryLater(const String & why)` and `makeCasWriteRetryLaterExceptionPtr(const String & why)`, and both carry `ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR` with the same message shape. topic: Recovery correctly fails closed when a

topic: Recovery grounding uses `ckpt.checkpointsnapshotid` as the
canonical_claim: Recovery grounding uses `_ckpt.checkpoint_snapshot_id` as the only snapshot base and `_ckpt.committed_through` as the inclusive frontier; it never derives a base, genesis, frontier, or stop condition from stream `LIST` results. Additionally, Stage A treats the ref stream as arithmetic: transaction ids are dense within each `(namespace, writer_epoch)` pair, recovery advances by exact-key reads, and a dead epoch is closed by an `EpochSeal` at the exact id that the dying predecessor's next PUT would have used; object listing is only a hint. Additionally, Recovery uses `_ckpt` plus an arithmetic tail and seal CAS-walk; LIST seeds candidates and supplies `_cleanup` markers but is never a census of durable records. Additionally, The ref-chain model covers per-namespace contiguous ids, in-band `slot-occupy` seals for epoch transitions, `_ckpt`-gated recovery, arithmetic fold intake, a durable frontier hold, and LIST-as-zero-trust-hint behavior through named sabotage and control configurations. Additionally, The v9 regression pair establishes that treating a scan as truth breaks recovery (`CaRefTableSnapshotLogCore_sab_scanistruth` is red) while omitting all records from the listing is harmless under arithmetic intake (`CaRefDeltaIntakeCore_v9_hintomission` is green). Additionally, For identical backend objects, full, empty, partial, and reordered listings must reconstruct the same logical state with zero recovery LIST requests; forged listed snapshots are not observed. Additionally, CAS recovery uses the exact checkpoint frontier through `chooseRecoveryGrounding`; `hint_log_ids` is not used, and neither `CasRefProtocol.cpp` nor `CasRefLedger.cpp` enumerates the ref stream with `Backend::list`. Additionally, Stale-but-honest reads create a true historical cut whose errors cause retention or delay, while a fabricated cut from omission under a seal can authorize unrecoverable destruction. Additionally, Paginated LIST cannot authorize destructive CAS decisions: a contract-compliant store may omit writes concurrent with an enumeration, but exact-key reads and conditional writes are trusted; LIST may only delay work. Additionally, No stream `LIST` result may decide genesis, committed membership, replay stop, `last_epoch_seal`, next transaction id, owner protection, or permission to delete. Additionally, The design rule that generalizes the LIST-trust resolution: any input feeding an irreversible action must be structurally unable to authorize it wrongly, it may only delay it. A stale-but-honest observation is a true cut from the past whose induced errors fall toward retention/latency and are closed forward by ordering and a final re-check at the destructive site; a fabricated cut (omission under a permanent seal) corresponds to no point in time and can authorize destruction. LIST is only used in roles that satisfy this (work bound, witness set, genesis hint); the trusted verbs (exact-key reads, conditional writes) carry everything else.

topic: `snapshotOf` rejects every non-`Live` state with
canonical_claim: `snapshotOf` rejects every non-`Live` state with `CORRUPTED_DATA` before constructing a snapshot DTO. Additionally, `snapshotOf` refuses every non-live state with `CORRUPTED_DATA` before DTO construction, and terminal replay tests preserve `Removed` plus its exact removal id.

topic: Writer recovery treats absent `ckpt.lifeepoch` as
canonical_claim: Writer recovery treats absent `_ckpt.life_epoch` as corruption for `Live` and `Removing`; it does not use the smallest listed log id as genesis, and `Creating` or catalog-absent lives are not recovered.

topic: The inclusive `committedthrough` frontier is the
canonical_claim: The inclusive `committed_through` frontier is the authoritative missing-slot witness and cannot be extended or shortened by listed ids.

topic: A selected listed object disappearing no
canonical_claim: A selected listed object disappearing no longer causes a fresh full-list restart; exact checkpoint re-reads resolve ambiguous observations and recovery fails closed when authority still requires a missing object.

topic: The modeled `ForgetTerminal` invariant requires completed
canonical_claim: The modeled `ForgetTerminal` invariant requires completed FORGET to have a latched fence and a `Vanished` state; removing trip 2 violates it because an in-flight reclaim can restore `Live` and `mayMutate() == TRUE`.

topic: The modeled `EarnedFarewell` invariant permits farewell
canonical_claim: The modeled `EarnedFarewell` invariant permits farewell only after a provable drain, and `OneWay` forbids transitions from `IdentityLost` or `Vanished` back to `Live` or `Transient`.

topic: `LocalObjectStorage::listObjects` uses an explicit-stack non-recursive walk
canonical_claim: `LocalObjectStorage::listObjects` uses an explicit-stack non-recursive walk with `error_code` overloads and a symlink guard to emulate object-store snapshot behavior while a sibling detached ref directory is removed.

topic: The one writer-side path that fails
canonical_claim: The one writer-side path that fails closed on corruption is a detected logical-hash collision: in store_blob_safely, when a writer reuses an existing logical-hash key it verifies the existing object's header hashes to the expected logical hash (verify(existing_hdr.logical_hash == H)); if it does not, the system quarantines the key and raises a hard error rather than silently papering over the mismatch, since silent reuse of a mis-verifying object would let corrupt or colliding content be served under a live ref.

topic: Key invariants: INV-OVER-COUNT-ONLY -- every failure
canonical_claim: Key invariants: INV-OVER-COUNT-ONLY -- every failure (lost fold, crashed leader, stale snap, duplicated records) delays reclamation but none accelerates a delete past the gates. INV-S3-COMPLETE -- S3 alone is both the durable truth and sufficient coordination; Keeper is an accelerator and total Keeper loss loses nothing and blocks nothing. INC-MONO -- for a fixed (ns, shard), every successive materialization of the shard object carries a strictly greater incarnation, closing ABA by construction. WriterEpochMonotoneUnique -- the epoch-object allocator never reissues a writer_epoch for a server_root_id, across crash/restart and across mount deletion.

topic: Backend safety depends on exact-token conditional
canonical_claim: Backend safety depends on exact-token conditional delete: a DELETE If-Match token with a wrong token MUST fail, not silently succeed; this is probed at startup and the disk fails closed if the backend does not enforce it. Bucket versioning must never be enabled on the CA prefix; versioning-suspended buckets are also rejected because a delete inserts a null delete marker, breaking the one-live-object model. A startup probe verifies this functionally.

topic: `gtestcasholeylistdetector.cpp`'s two kept tests (`OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever`, `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob`)
canonical_claim: `gtest_cas_holey_list_detector.cpp`'s two kept tests (`OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever`, `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob`) prove the arithmetic ref-intake's resilience to a holey LIST page independently of probe A, a class of coverage unrelated to and unaffected by probe A's removal.

topic: `CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla` checks `INVNODANGLING` and `INVNOORPHANEDGE` across
canonical_claim: `CaGcShardIncarnationCore.tla` checks `INV_NO_DANGLING` and `INV_NO_ORPHAN_EDGE` across 724,944 distinct states and proves that two orthogonal coordinates (a durable never-reused `incarnation` stamped at shard creation, and the pool-global GC `round`) are both necessary; three negative controls (`SabotageNewbornNoFloor`, `SabotagePathKeyedCursor`, `SabotageDeleteBeforeFold`) each show a counterexample when one coordinate is removed.

topic: Promote's publish-gate obligations (MR-1/MR-2/MR-3) apply only
canonical_claim: Promote's publish-gate obligations (MR-1/MR-2/MR-3) apply only to the non-tokened evidence/copy-forward dependency subset since EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE: MR-1 consults durable deleted-token history, not only a cached retired set; MR-2/F1 re-validates the dependency's current physical state (still present, still carrying the originally-observed token, not merely 'not condemned when first seen'); MR-3/F2 requires bottom-up tree publish so a manifest may publish only when every direct child is present and non-condemned at publish time. A tokened dependency gets zero promote-time re-validation against any of these.

topic: `INV-2` (precommit-first / reachability-before-content): the build-root
canonical_claim: `INV-2` (precommit-first / reachability-before-content): the build-root precommit must be published before any pool content GET/HEAD/PUT of the build's content; the full write ordering stages blobs into local temp files, then makes the edge-bearing manifest body durable via `stageManifest`, then lands the owner event via `precommitAdd`, and only then do blob uploads reach the pool. A writer dying mid-upload therefore leaves blobs whose edges already exist in a folded body, so there is no structural 'orphan blob' class — an object in `blobs/` with no edge-bearing body in history should be impossible and fsck may treat one as an anomaly.

topic: The CAS backend contract's `TOKEN ⟹
canonical_claim: The CAS backend contract's `TOKEN ⟹ CONTENT` requirement (a repeated token implies unchanged bytes) is the one item that cannot be probed cheaply and is therefore a documented, unverified assumption on every backend, not enforced by the capability probe.

topic: CAS's transient-vs-terminal exception classifier separates a
canonical_claim: CAS's transient-vs-terminal exception classifier separates a READ-plane and a WRITE-plane per an audit of every throw site tree-wide: the READ plane is the only one with destructive reach and had exactly two sites, of 106 GC-ref throw sites tree-wide 27 were transient (19 `NETWORK_ERROR`, 5 `INVALID_STATE`, 3 `ABORTED`); a write-once `ABORTED`-on-write-once site (718 occurrences) was judged a real defect while the deposition/fence family was deliberately left `INVALID_STATE` because recoding it to `ABORTED` would regress by escaping a backoff exemption.

topic: CAS's single true read-side correctness hole
canonical_claim: CAS's single true read-side correctness hole (labeled X1/R1, "missing read"): a ref-less/cross-node reader resolves ref to manifest to blob-location at plan time, discards the manifest, then performs a deferred, unpinned blob GET later; if the ref is dropped and GC completes condemn to pending to delete before that GET fires, a committed datum becomes unreadable mid-query (`NoSuchKey`). This is bounded to the write/GC plane being otherwise loss-free; the fix direction is an ephemeral reader pin folded into the GC mark/ack-floor union, or bounding query lifetime below the condemn-to-delete latency.

topic: CAS's security perimeter is exactly the
canonical_claim: CAS's security perimeter is exactly the S3 bucket credential: there is no intra-pool authorization, identities are self-asserted and unsigned, and blobs are shared pool-wide by content hash with no namespace in the blob key. Combined with non-cryptographic CityHash128 content-addressing and reads that never re-verify payload-against-key, this enables SEC-1 (High) collision poisoning: because dedup is HEAD-first and blobs are pool-global, an attacker who can craft a `CityHash128` collision can pre-seed a poisoned blob under the victim's future hash so a victim in a different table/tenant later writing the benign content dedups to the poison and reads attacker bytes, with all CRC checks passing (latent in a single-trust-domain pool, real the moment a pool is multi-tenant).

topic: SEC-8: provenance (`serverid`, timestamp, op, `buildid`)
canonical_claim: SEC-8: provenance (`server_id`, timestamp, op, `build_id`) and the `CasEvent` sink give a useful audit trail, but everything is self-asserted and forgeable by a pool-write adversary, so it is good for debugging and honest-fault forensics but not an integrity/attribution control against a malicious insider.

topic: SEC-9: blobs are plaintext table bytes
canonical_claim: SEC-9: blobs are plaintext table bytes; confidentiality relies entirely on S3 SSE + bucket policy + TLS, and content-addressing also makes content equality externally observable (same content maps to the same key), which deployments with confidential data across tenants in one pool should assume as an equality-leakage risk.

topic: The full set of code sites
canonical_claim: The full set of code sites sharing the renameParts -> Keeper-decision -> parts-commit slot audited for the part-durability-before-Keeper-commit fix is: `ReplicatedMergeTreeSink::commitPart` (INSERT, the only dedup-token site and hence the only silent-loss path), `renameMergedTemporaryPart` (merges), `MutateFromLogEntryTask::finalize`, `fetchPart`, `executeLogEntry`, `executeReplaceRange`, `replacePartitionFromImpl`, `movePartitionToTable`, `renameAndCommitEmptyParts`, and `createEmptyPartInsteadOfLost`; non-INSERT paths hit the same window but only cause replicated-log-entry re-execution churn, not acknowledged data loss.

topic: The ref-chain complete-cut design's generation-change safety
canonical_claim: The ref-chain complete-cut design's generation-change safety was confirmed to have no durable double-apply path: if the old PUT wins, the successor adopts it; if the successor's seal wins, the old PUT is rejected; if the generation changes before the old write is even sent, the old send is refused outright.

topic: The recommended fix for the CAS
canonical_claim: The recommended fix for the CAS `fsck` seal-awareness gap requires a point read of the authority for every known namespace, traversal of the complete seal-descriptor history, exact-`GET` verification of every referenced seal, and treating missing/malformed/regressed/mismatched pointer-vs-seal state as fatal `unchecked`/corruption rather than clean.

topic: The "natural black-box equivalence" test oracle
canonical_claim: The "natural black-box equivalence" test oracle requires a CA table to be byte-for-byte identical to a normal MergeTree table on the same data under active GC (stateless tests 04278/04279); divergence means a live blob was lost.

topic: Under the one-pipeline transaction design, CA
canonical_claim: Under the one-pipeline transaction design, CA manifest build, blob upload, and promote (remote I/O) deliberately run inside `MergeTreeData::Transaction::commit` under `lockParts()` (`MergeTreeData.cpp:8775/8792`); this is an accepted tradeoff per the spec's `Why There Is No Disk Precommit` rationale, not a regression, since moving remote I/O out of `data_parts` locking is a general commit-positioning/performance problem, not a CA-only correctness issue.

topic: CAS coordination state, including refs, mount
canonical_claim: CAS coordination state, including refs, mount leases, and GC state, is stored in the object store; backend mutual exclusion relies on conditional PUT/DELETE (If-None-Match/If-Match) and startup probes fail closed.

topic: Every behavior-changing phase that changes deletion
canonical_claim: Every behavior-changing phase that changes deletion semantics or GC safety must have a GREEN TLA+ model before implementation begins; negative controls must violate their named invariants.

topic: The amended resurrection invariant permits reading
canonical_claim: The amended resurrection invariant permits reading a condemned object only for verified copy-forward when a live committed manifest supplies `adoptEvidence`; it forbids blind PUT and `putIfAbsent` after a lost delete race.

topic: The inequality `minack ≤ K−1` prevents
canonical_claim: The inequality `min_ack ≤ K−1` prevents an entry condemned in pass K from graduating in that same pass, so the two-round condemnation pipeline follows from the round arithmetic.

topic: The queue's TLA+ posture treats a
canonical_claim: The queue's TLA+ posture treats a batch as a sequence of today's transitions committed atomically; any crash or conflict leaves a durable prefix, and the reachable durable states are a subset of those available from fast sequential `casPut` operations.

topic: The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`
canonical_claim: The TLA+ mount model adds `GcFence`, splits adopt into GET and CAS steps, permits late renewal after expiry, and checks `FENCE-COSTS-EPOCH` plus eventual remount liveness.

topic: Validate-on-hit retention compares every retained view
canonical_claim: Validate-on-hit retention compares every retained view with a fresh `resolveRef` result using `(manifest_id, mutable_files)`; ref-staleness semantics therefore match existing behavior without relying on complete mutation-site invalidation coverage.

topic: The accepted residual delta is that
canonical_claim: The accepted residual delta is that an externally deleted or tampered manifest may go undetected on a validated `CachedForLoad` hit until eviction, mismatch, `ForceFresh`, or `StrictValidate`; write-evidence and strict paths retain immediate body liveness validation.

topic: The combined fix is fail-close promote
canonical_claim: The combined fix is fail-close promote, idempotent republishRef re-drive, and retire-after-removal abandon; reachable refusal cases use ABORTED because LOGICAL_ERROR is reserved for impossible invariants.

topic: The backstop runs after the in-closure
canonical_claim: The backstop runs after the in-closure refresh and owner-liveness check, preventing consequential copy-forward work on an aborting path.

topic: The in-closure backstop is mandatory even
canonical_claim: The in-closure backstop is mandatory even if the pre-pass is refreshed opportunistically, because GC may advance again before the closure's fence-round refresh.

topic: Phase A deletes tokened per-leaf promote
canonical_claim: Phase A deletes tokened per-leaf promote revalidation and retained sources but keeps one presence check for every non-tokened leaf, including a fail-closed no-dep arm.

topic: Phase A removes the viewgate drain
canonical_claim: Phase A removes the view_gate drain because monotone retire-view installs and persistent graduated entries make in-closure reads see the required entries without the drain.

topic: Phase A removes the writer fence-round
canonical_claim: Phase A removes the writer fence-round refresh only when its TLA+ newborn-shard gate confirms the redundancy; the GC-side fence_round remains.

topic: Phase A removes redundant writer freshness
canonical_claim: Phase A removes redundant writer freshness machinery while retaining the dedup-adoption gate, promote owner check, and one non-tokened presence observation.

topic: GC freshness metadata is add-only: GC
canonical_claim: GC freshness metadata is add-only: GC may publish `Condemned` and remove metadata after confirmed deletion, but GC must never transition `Condemned` to `Clean` on a spare.

topic: The recovery seal is required because
canonical_claim: The recovery seal is required because `materialization_grace_ms` is an operational store allowance without a documented universal upper bound.

topic: The all-tree design closes B123's documented
canonical_claim: The all-tree design closes B123's documented fail-open in which a surgical single-file delete silently did nothing.

topic: The all-tree TLA+ safety argument refines
canonical_claim: The all-tree TLA+ safety argument refines a same-key repoint into `WDropRef` followed by `WPromote` on a scratch state, rather than modeling the whole repoint as a dedicated action.

topic: The Round-B plan required the absence-means-Clean
canonical_claim: The Round-B plan required the absence-means-Clean TLA+ gate to be green before any §5 code and required §5 code to land as one revertible commit.

topic: The MVCC atomic-write short-circuit must land
canonical_claim: The MVCC atomic-write short-circuit must land before routing the former mutable files through the content path; otherwise the tmp-plus-rename sequence would require unsupported rename-of-committed-file behavior.

topic: Refsnaplog objects are written through `putIfAbsentControlled`
canonical_claim: Refsnaplog objects are written through `putIfAbsentControlled` or `backend.putIfAbsent`, not `putDeterministicArtifact`, so their deterministic encoding is a correctness property rather than a byte-adoption gate.

topic: Part manifests are `Tolerant` and `Always`
canonical_claim: Part manifests are `Tolerant` and `Always` compressed but are not `Strict`, `PinnedRaw`, or a `putDeterministicArtifact` adoption gate; identity-keyed persistence uses `putIfAbsentControlled` and exchange re-hashes content.

topic: Deletes are applied to the overlay
canonical_claim: Deletes are applied to the overlay immediately rather than stored in a second replay list; therefore create → delete → create leaves the path present in the final overlay.

topic: `CasStore` decomposition is defined by state
canonical_claim: `CasStore` decomposition is defined by state and lock ownership: each extracted component moves its guarded state and mutexes wholesale, receives environment through constructor parameters or callbacks, and must not retain a `Pool &` back-reference.

topic: Publishing directly under final ref `<part>`
canonical_claim: Publishing directly under final ref `<part>` is rejected because a failure between clone commit and swap would leak an unreclaimed final ref and collide with the generic rename destination precheck; the `moving/<part>` prefix lets startup cleanup reclaim the transient ref.

topic: The ref-table COW change is scoped
canonical_claim: The ref-table COW change is scoped to `RefTableState::committed` and is intended to be pure performance work with byte-identical behavior.

topic: Review finding №27 is by design
canonical_claim: Review finding №27 is by design: `source absent && destination present → success` makes single-writer, deterministically-derived renames idempotent under re-drive.

topic: A CAS test that installs a
canonical_claim: A CAS test that installs a reference-capturing event sink must declare `std::vector<CasEvent> events` before the `Pool`, so reverse destruction order tears down the `Pool` before the sink target; explicitly resetting the `Pool` first is an equivalent but less local remedy.

topic: The safe test fix for `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell`
canonical_claim: The safe test fix for `CasPoolShutdown.UnresolvedWedgeSkipsFarewell` is to copy `store->layout()` by value before `store.reset()`; the ASan hit is unrelated to the product scheduler-pointer UAF called codex finding №8.

topic: Experiment E1 adds a `TrustedHistory` replay
canonical_claim: Experiment E1 adds a `TrustedHistory` replay mode that skips the O(N) `manifestAlreadyOwned` admission scan in release builds while retaining it as a `chassert` in debug and sanitizer builds; exact keyed preconditions remain enforced in both modes.

topic: Experiment E3 replaces whole-state scratch copies
canonical_claim: Experiment E3 replaces whole-state scratch copies with an undo-journal transaction layer that must preserve two-phase visibility and strong exception safety, while acknowledging allocation failure during rollback as an unrecoverable tradeoff.

topic: `TrustedHistory` was initially restricted to replay
canonical_claim: `TrustedHistory` was initially restricted to replay of transactions that had already passed `Full` validation at append time; all writer previews and append-time validation retained `Full` checking.

topic: The shipped E3 replay optimization applies
canonical_claim: The shipped E3 replay optimization applies `TrustedHistory` in place with no copy and accepts a poisoned local state on throw because replay returns the state only after full success; `Full` retains the two-phase scratch-copy guarantee.

topic: The corrected replay implementation deletes public
canonical_claim: The corrected replay implementation deletes public `ApplyMode` and keeps poison-on-throw in a private `RefTableState::applyTxnInPlace` reachable only from `replay`.

topic: The planned parallel commit snapshots parts
canonical_claim: The planned parallel commit snapshots parts into an index-addressable vector, preallocates outcome and exception slots, dispatches bounded worker loops, waits with `wait()` rather than `get()`, and performs rollback only after the inner runner scope drains.

topic: All CAS event emission routes through
canonical_claim: All CAS event emission routes through one reentrancy-safe serialized dispatcher, and ledger events are emitted after releasing ledger locks; per-component event locks are rejected because they can deadlock with reentrant sinks.

topic: The ref-lane fix must land before
canonical_claim: The ref-lane fix must land before publish-confirm work, and all three post-durable sites must install state without allocation: chunk commit apply, wedge-resolution apply, and wedge construction. Additionally, The ref-lane fix makes the interval between durable ref-log publication and runtime installation allocation-free at all three post-durable install sites, enforced by `DENY_ALLOCATIONS_IN_SCOPE` and reinforced with an apply-pending poison marker.

topic: A decommission path must not blindly
canonical_claim: A decommission path must not blindly bypass the mount-presence guard: minting epoch 1 over a live epoch-1 mount would recreate the forbidden same-pair twin and defeat live-member refusal.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: `confirmExactRef` must try-lock `state_mutex` while holding the ref queue mutex; failure to acquire it is treated as `Unknown` so confirmation never blocks pool-wide append admission behind recovery I/O.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Wedge retry is demand-driven: a permanently quiet wedged namespace retries on its next caller or an independently occurring remount, because the unresolved operation was never acknowledged.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The lease-blip fix is classified as a robustness fix: the induced timing kept the part `ACTIVE`, produced zero CA-log events and no `part_log` remediation row, while the residual double-blip risk remains named.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The recommended transient-classifier fix is to add `throwCasTransientUnavailable` beside `throwCasWriteRetryLater` in `Backend/CasRequestControl.cpp:190-201`, minting `NETWORK_ERROR` for `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage.cpp:1111`, `:1163`, and `CasMountRuntime.cpp:106`; this changes no upstream files.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The apply-marker lock belongs at each call site rather than inside `armApplyPending`, because `forceWedgeForTest` already calls it while holding `state_mutex`; the helper remains `noexcept`, allocation-free, and lock-free with a documented locking precondition.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Recovery must not fall back to `hint_log_ids.front()` or fabricate `life_epoch` with `value_or`.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Fsck's namespace and life universe must come from one validated catalog snapshot; backend listings may discover physical objects within that universe or report extra orphaned objects.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: GC, ref cleanup, namespace cleanup, fsck, and decommission should consume one immutable `GcNamespacePlan` or one shared catalog snapshot and must not independently re-read catalog state.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The catalog's advantage over LIST is atomic completeness as of one object-version cut, not freshness; protocol closes staleness after the cut but cannot recover a namespace never named by an incomplete LIST.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Canonical life-qualified objects whose life is not the current catalog life are inert debris; malformed or unparseable keys remain anomalies; an absent or undecodable initialized Stage-B catalog stops creation, removal, and GC.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The LIST-derived fsck snapshot oracle was removed; `FsckClass::SnapshotOracleMismatch`, its report fields, its hard-findings row, and the corresponding `CommandFsck` failure path are absent from production code.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Verification agents receive claim and cluster JSON but not the source documents; evidence must come from code at HEAD rather than from the statement that a document says the claim.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: A random five-percent adversarial audit rechecks `done` and `stale` verdicts because a false `done` can lose work and a false `stale` can lose knowledge.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: A reachable state handled by code must not be guarded by `chassert`: the handler is the fail-closed behavior, and an assertion above it otherwise makes sanitizer/debug builds abort while release builds execute the handler.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: When a function's returned aggregate element type, member count, or member order changes, every structured-binding call site such as `auto [a, b]` must be audited because C++17 can silently rebind fields without a compile error.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The mount model's honest `RemintEpoch` path over-approximates production because it omits the code precondition `serverRootSubtreeEmpty`; the model's honest `FenceCostsEpoch` counterexample is therefore conservative rather than proof that production reaches the same state.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The recovery-generation model identifies an operation by `<< actor, generation, op >>`; using only `<< actor, generation >>` aliases distinct same-generation operations and can hide an ack for bytes that were never written.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The ref-lane implementation replaced nested apply-marker and durable-floor encodings with `RefLaneState{Ready,Writing,Wedged,NeedsRecovery,Closed,Faulted}`; confirmation is `Ready`-only and terminal `Closed`/`Faulted` states are non-retriable.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: CAS design work treats a proof of correctness as requiring an executable, reproducible counterexample: a test must be able to fail. A relink proved only by a flat blob count is worthless because a byte fetch onto a content-addressed disk also dedups and produces the same flat count, so that test cannot distinguish the mechanism under test from a working fallback.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: CAS operations must fail closed under ambiguity: an operation that may have landed must not be treated as one that did not.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: `blob_storage_log` records object writes and deletes but not LIST calls, so the observed evidence bounds timing without identifying whether the listing failure was a dropped page, a boundary error, or another store behavior.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: A `ca-surgeon` safety argument must be re-derived when the storage shape being changed is within that argument's scope.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The cache is a memoized access layer over already-valid CAS operations, not a new CAS protocol component.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The cache design keeps public APIs small, keeps cache code outside CAS protocol logic where possible, makes mutation side effects local, preserves the call graph when disabled, and does not weaken CAS invariants or TLA+ assumptions.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: `PartFolderView` must not call back into `ContentAddressedMetadataStorage`, mutate `Cas::Store`, or perform object-store I/O.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: In disabled mode, `getView` still resolves refs and reads manifests, writes still use `CachedPartFolderAccess`, and correctness and side effects remain identical, but the one-`GET` performance guarantee is absent.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The cache facade erases the affected view after a successful `updateMutableFiles`, `dropRef`, `promoteBuild`, or `dropNamespace` operation.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Cache insertion captures a local sequence before loading and publishes the view only when that sequence is unchanged, preventing a stale in-flight read from repopulating after a local write.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The cache mutex must not be held during `resolveRef`, `readManifest`, `HEAD`, `GET`, or decode, and single-flight must be scoped per `(namespace, ref)` or `ManifestId` rather than globally.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: CAS blob content hashes use CityHash128 consistently with MergeTree file checksums, while tree or manifest identity also uses CityHash128 where other higher-level identities commonly use SipHash128; the review recommends documenting or revisiting that choice under the collision model.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: A valid successor seal must remain the conclusive rejection when an old I/O result returns after a generation bump, and the superseded runtime must not acknowledge, install, or publish it

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: RunFile block and footer CRC32C should remain until RunRef.checksum is either verified as a full-run artifact hash before trust or removed or demoted before release

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: CAS fsck classifies canonical physical keys absent from the catalog at a post-listing observation cut as soft FsckClass::JanitorPending, with report fields namespace_janitor_pending, namespace_janitor_pending_bytes, and namespace_janitor_pending_lives; these fields are excluded from kFsckHardFindings.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: CasFsck.cpp uses observe-then-cut classification: it buffers canonical candidates during the physical LIST, reads a fresh catalog cut after listing completes, and classifies candidates against that cut to protect concurrent namespace creation.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The two holey-LIST tests `OmittedRemoveRecordIsSkippedForever` and `OmittedActivationNeverPermitsDeletingALiveBlob` are retained because they cover skipped-transaction retention-leak and data-loss behavior independently of probe A.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The anomaly and carried-hold terms in `suppress_destructive` are structural defense-in-depth: in current in-fold paths they co-fire with frontier incompleteness and cannot be isolated by the existing test seams.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: `RefPlan` has a private mandatory constructor, is non-assignable, exposes const views only, and has neither mutable `foldState` nor a destructive `releaseFoldStates` operation.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The sole ref-plan builder consumes an rvalue `RoundInput` and moves its scan and catalog cut into `RefPlan`; fold, the store-quality probe, DEFER accounting, frontier/publication, and healthy rebuild receive the bound plan only.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Raw `RoundInput` construction is private to `Gc` and the narrow named `tests::buildRefWalkPlanForTest` wrapper, preventing arbitrary scan/catalog pairs from bypassing the production binding boundary.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The authoritative `CaRefLaneCore` model composes the existing single six-state append lane with a bounded identity/cache submodel containing two runtime ids, two durable life ids, one non-authoritative name slot, one old handle, immutable identity records, per-runtime cache/durable markers, one delayed-invalidation target, and fence state.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: An already-issued stale request may land only while its adopted proof remains current; the B-drained takeover trace is a helping barrier rather than atomic revocation of an independent catalog CAS.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The copy `const RefTableState before = state;` in `E3AdmitsPreviewLeavesStateByteIdentical` must remain an independent snapshot because `state` is mutated later for byte-identical comparison.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: The TLA+ model collapses the real `armMountFence .. noteRemounted` interval into one atomic reclaim action because the op gate refuses durable admission while the state is not `Live` and older fence generations fail revalidation.

topic: correctness
canonical_claim: Canonical catalog-absent objects are inert debris that must never damage data; fsck therefore needs a grammar-discriminated `janitor_pending` class rather than treating all such debris as a hard corruption finding.

topic: correctness

RPL-3 was judged safe in practice because the sender cannot remove a part until it receives an ack, which the receiver gives only after a successful write.

topic: design-history

RPL-2 (ZK/CAS ref divergence on partial commit) is judged not a CAS-specific issue but general ReplicatedMergeTree partial-commit behavior that the project already knows how to resolve (via detached-parts handling). RPL-4 (`to_detached` relink disabled, always streams bytes) is accepted as a possible real performance issue to recheck, believed to use the same mechanics as a normal fetch. RPL-5 (no dedicated CAS integration tests for quorum/SYNC REPLICA/cloneReplica) is accepted as coverage debt comparable to other ClickHouse features, mitigated by all stateless tests passing successfully against a CAS-backed server.

topic: EBR (Epoch-Based Reclamation) GC core -- writers holding a pin epoch (an ephemer
canonical_claim: An EBR (Epoch-Based Reclamation) GC core -- writers holding a pin epoch (an ephemeral Keeper node), GC advancing through safe_epoch/commit_epoch/birth_epoch and waiting for quiescence, with generations on blob keys (blobs/<H>/<g>) as the ABA guard -- was rejected because a stuck or wedged writer held down safe_epoch and stalled reclamation of all dropped parts across all writers, Keeper was required for correctness, and a long-running INSERT could delay GC for its entire duration. topic: Whole-object copy-on-write for `RefTableState

topic: Three fixes for the GC-registry monotone-growth problem were rejected before the
canonical_claim: Three fixes for the GC-registry monotone-growth problem were rejected before the shard-incarnation redesign: (1) writer deregisters at `dropNamespace` — unsafe because the removal `-1` in-degree edges would be lost if the namespace vanished from discovery before GC folded that window; (2) GC hard-deregisters when 'empty + settled' — indistinguishable from a live table between CREATE and its first INSERT; (3) shard-object deletion on the path-keyed cursor — an ABA hazard where a recreated shard resets `shard_version` to 0 and an old sealed cursor silently skips the new incarnation's events.

topic: Rejected writer-protocol designs

canonical_claim: E4 (flat-vector base for RefTableState) was REVERTED after implementation: it only cleared Materialize's asymptotic cost 2x (O(NlogN)->O(N)) on a cost that is per-flush, never trace-visible, and N-budget-bounded, so simplicity won over the marginal gain.

topic: Keeping a permanent `Retired` catalog row instead of the transient `RemovalReady

canonical_claim: Inferring damage from entry-less debris was rejected because legal debris and a fabricated missing catalog entry are physically indistinguishable; adding more classifier branches cannot create information that was never persisted.

topic: first proposed fix for the deposed-leader stray-Clean defect (Fix 1
canonical_claim: The first proposed fix for the deposed-leader stray-Clean defect (Fix 1: couple `clearSparedMeta` to adoption by moving it after the winning `gc/state` CAS, plus a `condemn_round` guard) was proven insufficient by a second model consult: a stale, paused leader can issue the destructive exact-token `deleteExact(t1)` pre-CAS from an older adopted snapshot, so a fresh leader's legitimately-adopted post-CAS clear still lets a writer reuse `t1` and the stale leader's redelete kills the live reuse, because the final `gc/state` CAS fences adoption, not pre-CAS side effects.

topic: ref-lease-exclusivity rev
canonical_claim: The ref-lease-exclusivity rev.6 proposal left four open questions for review at draft time: whether a 30s `T_mat` unclean-handover penalty is acceptable in production given rustfs/MinIO/real-S3 request-lifetime differences; whether the eager recovery snapshot should also run on clean mounts with a large inherited tail; whether the seal's wedge/single-in-flight invariant may be hard-required via chassert plus release fail-close at the lane level; and confirming that the interim mechanical patch (aged trigger, copy-once replay, threshold 256) lands regardless of the proposal's outcome.

topic: generation handoff leak

topic: pending manifest preservation

topic: abandoned precommit parked shard

topic: concurrent GC leader artifacts
canonical_claim: Concurrent explicit GC leaders could orphan unreachable content blobs and part-manifests while preserving safety (`fsck dangling=0`): a deposed leader wrote a final-key fold seal under `gc/gen/<gen>/fold_seal` before the lease-guarded `gc/state` CAS, a divergent `putIfAbsent` made the losing leader throw `ABORTED` without advancing state, and the winner's seal was never re-adopted so owner-removal events were not re-folded. Attempt-scoped generations keyed by `(gen, attempt = lease.seq)` hide unadopted artifacts and fix this.

topic: D1 originated because `dropNamespace` tombstoned shard contents but never remove

topic: dryrun reachability divergence

topic: Racing multipart copies can produce different multipart ETags, leaving the losin
canonical_claim: Racing multipart copies can produce different multipart ETags, leaving the losing writer's recorded token stale and making exact-token deletion unable to reclaim the object.

topic: Lazy scheduler-creation sites can resurrect a `gc_scheduler` after shutdown
canonical_claim: Lazy scheduler-creation sites can resurrect a `gc_scheduler` after shutdown; a full fix requires retaining a shared pointer for rounds and gating lazy creation with a started flag.

topic: condemn marker write failures
canonical_claim: Swallowed or failed Condemned-marker writes can let a writer adopt a retired token or treat absent/Clean metadata as live, after which a later exact-token GC delete can remove a blob still referenced by a committed edge or newly referenced blob; task T1 fixed the load-bearing gate in commits `21a6051e8ff` and `12ae454e7f2`.

topic: parent-union generation pruning
canonical_claim: Pre-CAS generation or retention pruning based only on the proposed seal can delete a run or data still referenced by a winning concurrent leader's parent seal or by the currently adopted GC snapshot, permanently wedging GC with `CORRUPTED_DATA` in `PriorEdgeCursor`; task T3 fixed it by using the parent-union-proposed generation set in commit `883c8f92d66`.

topic: Review finding №18 is real

topic: Review finding №19c is latent local-CA data loss across restart

topic: Review finding №28 is real
canonical_claim: Review finding №28 is real: `Pool::beginPartWrite` can register a build sequence before construction fails, permanently pinning the GC `minActive` retention floor until remount.

topic: S31's `ca-gc-dryrun` failure was caused by a card oracle comparing a single-roun
canonical_claim: S31's `ca-gc-dryrun` failure was caused by a card oracle comparing a single-round `dry_count` with cumulative multi-round `deleted_total`; `Gc::previewDeletes` already iterates every shard.

topic: late-log clamp starvation
canonical_claim: A poison late log causes repeated failing reads that clamp its key; every healthy GC round records `CasGcClampSuppressedPasses:1`, clamp suppression skips the orphan-manifest sweep pass that would call `reportLateLogsIfAny`, and late-log detection is therefore structurally starved while the clamp persists.

topic: Issue [Altinity/ClickHouse#2052](https
canonical_claim: Issue [Altinity/ClickHouse#2052](https://github.com/Altinity/ClickHouse/issues/2052) does not reproduce on HEAD because commit `318291fe5e5` moved orphan-manifest ownership recovery to `recoverRefTable`, which `CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp` still uses through `recoverRefTableDetailed`.

topic: shipped TLA+ confirm model permits a dangle when one durable journal record is o

topic: FSCK/GC residual blobs
canonical_claim: The FSCK/GC disagreement involved 56 blobs: `ca-fsck` classified them as `AwaitingGc` with `dangling=0`, while GC repeatedly reported zero candidates and never drained them; each present blob had no live reference and exactly one residual source edge in the adopted in-degree run, the corresponding manifest no longer existed, GC marked zero candidates across 1,062 rounds, and the edges traced to four `tmp-fetch_*` refs published and dropped within 43 ms.

topic: In the retention direction, omitting a ref-log removal record can advance the cu

topic: In the deletion direction, omitting a second live owner's activation `+1` while
canonical_claim: In the deletion direction, omitting a second live owner's activation `+1` while folding the first owner's removal can make GC compute zero in-degree for a blob still referenced by a committed manifest and delete that blob.

topic: `BlobDelta
canonical_claim: `BlobDelta::txn_ordinal` must remain the last member unless positional aggregate initializers are converted, because inserting it before `remove` silently rebinds `BlobDelta{ref, source_id, remove}` and turns removals into activations.

topic: residual `+1` can arise either because its `-1` ref-log was omitted and the curs
canonical_claim: A residual `+1` can arise either because its `-1` ref-log was omitted and the cursor sealed past it, or because the `-1` reached the reducer before its `+1`; the latter is counted by `CasGcUnmatchedRemoveDeltas` and is a separate investigation.

topic: initial arithmetic fold walk caused an unbounded-round liveness regression

topic: REBUILD manifest-less orphans
canonical_claim: REBUILD cannot safely reclaim manifest-less orphan blobs while a live manifest can be hidden from `LIST`: it can currently condemn a physically listed blob when its live manifest is omitted, and a rebuild that condemns nothing cannot reclaim a blob whose manifest no longer exists anywhere because that blob has no row in the rebuilt baseline; such blobs remain fsck `unaccounted` until the authoritative R4 build/upload registry exists.

topic: Before incarnation qualification, `groupRefKeys` grouped listed ref keys by `par

topic: orphan sweep folded edges

topic: `CasGc

topic: uncataloged shard-0 cursor is re-added to every GC round, so its recurring anoma

topic: persisted fold cursor is keyed only by namespace and shard, so a recreated names
canonical_claim: The persisted fold cursor is keyed only by namespace and shard, so a recreated namespace can inherit a predecessor incarnation's sequence boundary and omit the new incarnation's first positive owner edges from the GC baseline.

topic: Deleting the perpetual `_files` janitor would make a single omitted `LIST` resul

topic: RustFS ref-log omission

topic: gc-defer-round-behavior
canonical_claim: DEFER leaves the sealed `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)` unchanged, so journals accumulate naturally from the old sealed cursor and a later FOLD processes the accumulated deltas without new persisted accumulator state. Additionally, `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds` bounds batching so every accumulated delta is folded within a bounded number of rounds; a due destructive decision also forces a FOLD. Additionally, A deferred GC round reports `RoundReport::deferred=true`, emits a round event with `outcome = "deferred"`, and leaves the sealed generation pinned without fold, delete, or round-commit CAS; a FOLD resets the leader-local defer counter. Additionally, Phase 4 Lever A lets a GC round re-adopt the sealed in-degree generation as DEFER when cheap pre-fold signals show no destructive decision; due graduation forces a fold, and the safety gate is `CaGcRoundDeferCore`.

topic: The modeled GcStoppedAfterForget invariant holds even

topic: The magic_enum enum_range for ASTSystemQuery Type
