topic: A build heartbeat is durable in
canonical_claim: A build heartbeat is durable in the pool before the first blob PUT via the pool-wide gc/hb pulse plus the writer's mount object build-watermark floor; there is no separate builds/<build_id> object in the current layout.

topic: Regular GC deletion outcomes are classified
canonical_claim: Regular GC deletion outcomes are classified as deleted | absent | replaced (412 = resurrection won) | spared, and retire entries are dropped only on confirmed outcomes.

topic: resurrect-reupload token handling
canonical_claim: The force-Read override HEADs only fire from `closeBlob` on hashes touched in the current fold window (`cur_edges == 0`); `settleRetiredBelow`'s quiescent-entry path never issues a HEAD and must not be changed to do so. The resurrect-reupload fix keys blob condemnation on `(hash, current token)` instead of only on the hash, and re-condemns a current token when a touched hash has net in-degree zero and a prior retired token differs. The resurrect-reupload fix makes `closeBlob` HEAD the current token when a prior retired entry reaches zero in-degree and condemns the current token if it differs from the retired token, matching `CaIncarnationCore`'s `GRetire` behavior. The resurrect-replaced repair adds one HEAD only for a touched condemned transition; quiescent graduation through `settleRetiredBelow` takes no additional HEAD.

topic: On a resurrect supersede the fold
canonical_claim: On a resurrect supersede the fold keeps exactly one retired entry per hash: the stale entry is dropped, not kept alongside the fresh re-condemn, and the retired list stays hash-sorted.

topic: Sharded GC correctness was validated by
canonical_claim: Sharded-GC correctness was validated by S15: identical oracle checksums and `dangling=0` under both `gc_shards=1` (default) and `gc_shards=2`, with reducer memory flat (0.60->0.61 GB) and orphan backlog fully drained in both configurations.

topic: Under suppress_destructive both the manifest_deletes phase
canonical_claim: Under `suppress_destructive`, both the `manifest_deletes` phase and the orphan sweep are gated closed: `mf_cleanup_now` is an empty map, and the orphan-sweep delete loop consumes `folded.orphan_sweep.nominations`, which is empty because `planManifestCursorPage` is only invoked when `!suppress_destructive`.

topic: The frontier round s universe is
canonical_claim: The frontier round's "universe" is exactly every `Live`/`Removing` row of the round's own frozen catalog cut and nothing else; an older comment defining it as "hint ∪ sealed cursors ∪ catalog Live/Removing entries" is stale and contradicts the code, which implements only the catalog-cut definition.

topic: GC s raw baseline rebuild condemns
canonical_claim: GC's raw baseline rebuild condemns nothing: it only rebuilds cursors and edges. An earlier version ended the pass by LISTing `blobs/` and condemning every physically-present body outside the rebuilt edge set, but this was found unsafe (r5-finding-4) because both legs of the traversal (owner replay and the trimmed-but-live manifest pass) are listing-driven, so a store that omits a durable key from one enumeration hides a live owner while the same pass condemns the blob that owner pins — an observed real failure mode (the `0x1430c` shape), not a hypothetical.

topic: Patch parts lightweight deletes are first
canonical_claim: Patch parts / lightweight deletes are first-class GC reachability roots: a patch manifest references the base part's patched data columns plus its own delta blobs, and while a patch ref is active it transitively keeps alive both its own delta blobs and the base blobs it references, even if the base part is otherwise superseded, provided the MARK walk treats patch manifests as roots. When a patch is materialized into the base via merge, the patch ref is released and its uniquely-owned delta blobs become sweepable. Patch-on-content-addressed-base is flagged as not yet fully model-checked in the v3 design's residual-risk list.

topic: A stateless ref less reader that
canonical_claim: A stateless/ref-less reader that attaches by reading the catalog and registers no `/parts` ref is invisible to the per-process `use_count()==1` MARK-union fence, which is a valid cross-node fence only for replicas holding a `/parts` ref; owning replicas can release refs after `old_parts_lifetime` (480s) mid-SELECT, sweeping the manifest/blobs out from under the read. The preferred fix is an ephemeral reader pin (a Keeper node or equivalent) created at query start naming the parts/snapshot read, auto-released on session end/crash; this is distinct from the lost-replica timeout, which is a genuine leak needing a separate long-dead-replica reaping rule.

topic: clamp suppression
canonical_claim: `CaGcAckFloorCore.tla`'s `SabotageClampNoSuppress` config, which removes the `~clampedL` graduation guard, reproduces the 2026-07-03 night incident of 31 dangling blobs as an `INV_NO_DANGLE` counterexample; the shipped clamp-suppression guard (`suppress_destructive` gating `Gc::graduationDue`, `CasGc.cpp:1360`) blocks graduation and pending deletes while any shard is clamped, so held refs persist in `landed` until a later clamp-free pass consumes them. If any fold pass records a clamp anomaly, destruction is suppressed: no graduations or redeletes occur, pending entries carry `UNCHANGED`, condemn/spare continue, and deletes resume on the first clamp-free pass; the pass emits a warning and increments `CasGcClampSuppressedPasses`.

topic: putDeterministicArtifact is the write once helper
canonical_claim: `putDeterministicArtifact` is the write-once helper for GC objects whose bytes are a pure function of their inputs (source-edge runs, fold seals): a `putIfAbsent` precondition failure is resolved by reading the existing object back and comparing bytes — byte-equal means the writer's own replay landed and is adopted as a no-op, while divergent bytes throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` as an impossible case. It is deliberately not used for observation-bearing artifacts like GC outcome logs, which use first-durable-write-wins byte-adopt semantics instead, and never for blob bodies because the fresh-tag rule makes two attempts of the same logical create legitimately differ.

topic: In GC sharding a shard with
canonical_claim: In GC sharding, a shard with an empty delta bucket and no condemned entries in the parent summary copies the parent's run references verbatim ("pure carry", zero run I/O); a missing parent summary entry on a non-fresh pool is `CORRUPTED_DATA`, never silently treated as zero.

topic: generation pruning
canonical_claim: Generation pruning (GC phase 13) keeps the last `gc_snap_generations_to_keep` generations (default 3; 0 keeps everything for forensics) and deletes wholesale by LIST-and-delete-everything under the generation prefix, bounded to 64 generations per round. A generation still referenced by the live seal is skipped but the cursor still advances past it regardless, so leak-freedom depends entirely on the post-CAS hand-off reclaim in phase 14. Implemented retention skips at generation granularity and advances `snap_pruned_through` over every visited generation; when a reference moves off a skipped generation, hand-off deletes the whole `gc/gen/<g>/` prefix rather than one run, preventing leaks of the rest of that generation's artifacts.

topic: namespace removal cleanup
canonical_claim: Namespace removal has no physical-empty handshake: the writer changes the catalog row from `Live` to `Removing`, appends the exact ref removals plus a `RemoveNamespace` op, and deletes nothing itself. GC's fold attaches cleanup evidence to that opaque life row, and only a later GC invocation's pre-fold drain exact-CAS-deletes the matching `Removing` catalog row before any successor plan can be published; the perpetual namespace janitor and orphan-manifest sweep reclaim the physical debris independently, and a same-name birth waits only for the catalog row to disappear. Namespace removal deletes lifecycle metadata only; it has no `suppress_destructive` input and performs no physical deletion, leaving `_ckpt`, stream objects, `_files`, and other dead-life objects to the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor. Catalog deletion does not require physical emptiness: `_ckpt`, stream, `_snap`, and `_files` residue may remain for the perpetual janitor or a family-specific sweep. Lifecycle physical cleanup is not part of the pre-fold drain: `suppress_destructive` does not govern it, and the perpetual `cas/ns/` janitor plus orphan-manifest sweep own physical debris. Removal completion performs no namespace-owned physical LIST, physical delete, physical-empty proof, or second deletion window; `_ckpt`, stream, and namespace-file residue is leak-only janitor work, while orphan manifests remain the orphan sweep's work.

topic: Attribution of the night s 11
canonical_claim: Attribution of the night's 11 concurrent GC clamps was: RustFS returned false 404s on HEAD during a metacache storm caused by the `rustfs#3231` overwrite-leak's directory bloat (00:37-00:55); the clamps rose with the storm and self-released when it subsided (~01:01), and the bodies the false 404s claimed were missing had never actually been deleted (no `tree_delete` for the pinned manifests). The full causal chain is: leak -> directory bloat -> metacache storm -> false 404s on HEAD -> GC clamps -> (pre-fix) graduation proceeding over unfolded landed events -> dangling blobs.

topic: CAS probe A the ref scan
canonical_claim: CAS probe A (the ref-scan disagreement detector) reports each hole with the ref-log id and its direction: holes missing from the fold's own (second) scan are explainable by concurrent deletion, but holes missing from the pre-fold (first) scan are not — the object existed at the second walk and its id sits below what the first walk had already observed, so the first walk should have returned it.

topic: The Stage B strategic review concentration
canonical_claim: The Stage B strategic-review concentration proposal's replacement namespace-removal sequence is: (1) catalog transitions Live to Removing; (2) the fenced owner appends the terminal record; (3) GC folds the terminal record and performs one bounded cleanup pass; (4) GC writes a stable retirement marker derived only from RootNamespace; (5) GC durably publishes a fold seal with that namespace's cursor pruned; (6) GC exact-deletes `_ckpt`; (7) catalog entry deletion happens last.

topic: Ordering the retirement marker before _ckpt
canonical_claim: Ordering the retirement marker before `_ckpt` deletion means even catalog loss cannot turn a namespace-removal window into a fresh birth; creation must check both the retirement marker and the namespace's `_ckpt` by exact key before admission and refuse if either exists; a listing omission can leak old objects but cannot make a retired namespace visible again because it is never re-admitted.

topic: Even under the no namespace reuse
canonical_claim: Even under the no-namespace-reuse simplification, catalog authority, the `Creating` publication exclusion, the `Removing` positive-ownership exclusion, the exact-next frontier probe, durable holds, and the delete-site in-degree re-read must not be cut, because they prevent data loss independently of rebirth; a temporary "refuse while old objects survive, retry after GC" rule does not substitute for them since LIST cannot certify old-object absence.

topic: C2 s widening past its three
canonical_claim: C2's widening past its three originally-named sites is justified because `marker_key` is the guard that the physical manifest and verbatim passes consult, so they cannot run without a resolved life; the still-sentinel-keyed `namespaceFilesPrefix` is correct because every writer of namespace files is also sentinel-keyed, making that layer Task 6's responsibility rather than a C2 leftover.

topic: The GC round s exact durable
canonical_claim: The GC round's exact durable key layout: `gc/state` (controller state, one per pool, strict fail-closed CAGT-magic proto), `gc/hb` (advisory heartbeat, fixed 24-byte binary), `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/fold_seal` (write-once fold seal), `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/.../<round>/<shard>` (retire outcome log), `cas/refs/<ns>/_log/<txn_id>` (ref log txn), `cas/refs/<ns>/_snap/<id>.proto` (ref snapshot).

topic: source-edge reachability set
canonical_claim: Blob reachability is source-edge set membership, not a counter: one source edge is (BlobRef, source_id) where source_id = CityHash128(namespace + ref + path), with 0 reserved as the sentinel key for kCondemned rows. The edge set is idempotent under re-fold, so retries and competing attempts produce byte-identical runs. Blob in-degree is derived from a folded set of source-edge deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)` rather than stored as a mutable counter; set semantics can delay reclamation but cannot accelerate deletion.

topic: Spared means a condemned blob s
canonical_claim: "Spared" means a condemned blob's in-degree recovered because a publish re-referenced it; the retired entry is dropped and recovery wins even past the graduation floor. "Forgotten" has no live meaning in this subsystem — the memory-noted GForget/GcSnap::forget design is superseded by pruneSupersededGenerations (wholesale generation retention).

topic: There is no crash resume step
canonical_claim: There is no crash-resume step in the GC round: the whole round commits in the single `gc/state` CAS at the end, so a crashed pass leaves only attempt-scoped debris under its own unadopted lease.seq, never adopted and later reclaimed by `pruneSupersededGenerations` or the Task-7 hand-off. Every pre-CAS destructive action is justified by previously-published durable state (`delete_pending`), making replay under a fresh attempt idempotent.

topic: The orphan manifest sweep gates deletion
canonical_claim: The orphan-manifest sweep gates deletion by `prefixEligible`, a durable watermark-only fact (`min_active > build_sequence`, or the retired sentinel `min_active==UINT64_MAX`, or an older epoch; a missing watermark means NOT eligible), and skips any key still in `activeManifestKeys(ns)` (committed + live precommits + manifests removed above the durable fold cursor). It never GETs a condemned body to revive it.

topic: Stage B Task 5 s restated
canonical_claim: Stage B Task 5's restated invariant: no same-name namespace entry can be created while any GC-held state (cursor, cleanup item, seal row) for the previous life survives; under this ordering, the catalog entry for a dropped table survives until the terminal record folds (a GC-round latency), so `CREATE TABLE` of a just-dropped name is refused — today as a `LOGICAL_ERROR` (`Pool/CasRefCatalog.cpp:236`) — until the next fold, which will burn stateless CI lanes that drop-and-recreate names constantly.

topic: Capture at deposition recording NamespaceLifeId at
canonical_claim: Capture-at-deposition (recording `NamespaceLifeId` at fold time rather than re-deriving it from the catalog) is mandatory because the stale-leader TLA+ sabotage shows that re-deriving the incarnation after rebirth targets the new life directly, causing data loss.

topic: A removed namespace whose only residue
canonical_claim: A removed namespace whose only residue is `_files` promotes its cleanup item to `Completed` on the first fold, so the janitor cannot key its reclaim logic off `Pending` state alone.

topic: Non per namespace fold seal capacity
canonical_claim: Non-per-namespace fold-seal capacity terms (`btr` per run segment, `cnd` per gc-shard) are untouched by the removal-ordering decision and do not disappear along with the Σ-index-set capacity argument.

topic: Probe A detects CAS ref prefix
canonical_claim: Probe A detects CAS ref-prefix LIST incompleteness via two independent enumerations per GC round (the pre-fold defer scan and fold's own enumeration); it compares per-namespace id sets and reports a hole only when the id is below the OTHER enumeration's own maximum for that namespace, which excludes ordinary in-flight appends between the two walks.

topic: Probe A has two documented blind
canonical_claim: Probe A has two documented blind spots it does not catch: a hole that reproduces identically in both enumerations, and a namespace dropped wholesale from one enumeration (no `ref_tables` entry, so the comparison loop never visits it); widening the witness rule to use the pre-scan's own maximum was considered and rejected because it would permanently block the cursor on a namespace whose logs were legitimately cleaned between the walks.

topic: stale_edge_verdict returns unchecked on any partial
canonical_claim: `stale_edge_verdict` returns `unchecked` on any partial scan, with positive findings still checked first, because a partial scan can only weaken a proof of absence, never invalidate evidence of presence.

topic: The chosen fix Fix 4 for
canonical_claim: The chosen fix (Fix 4) for the deposed-leader stray-Clean defect makes GC freshness metadata add-only: GC never transitions Condemned to Clean on a spare (the spare-side `clearSparedMeta` call and helper are removed); only a writer that has displaced the body with a fresh incarnation token publishes Clean, via `uploadFromSource` + `writeResurrectMetaClean`/`copyForwardFromCondemned`. Accepted cost: a spared hash stays Condemned until a writer resurrects it (write amplification on recurring-hash churn); normal reads never consult the meta so this is safe.

topic: The hot cold layout split changed
canonical_claim: The hot/cold layout split changed GC discovery to GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/, making discovery proportional to ref shards rather than manifest backlog.

topic: GC runs as a background lease
canonical_claim: GC runs as a background lease-holder loop and its safety does not depend on leadership uniqueness; concurrent or stale leaders may duplicate work but must not mis-delete.

topic: The advisory GC heartbeat is stored
canonical_claim: The advisory GC heartbeat is stored in `gc/hb` as `{owner, hb_seq}` and is advanced independently of round progress to prevent a live slow leader from being falsely stolen.

topic: over-protective baseline rebuild
canonical_claim: A forced GC rebuild over-protects unowned manifests that are not provably build-dead, preferring bounded leaks over violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY` through under-counting. GC baseline rebuild is deliberately over-protective rather than under-protective: a build alive across journal trim has no journal evidence, so its manifests look unowned; the rebuild includes edges for every unowned manifest that is not provably build-dead, over-protecting rather than risking under-count. An unowned manifest that later dies with no journal evidence leaks its blob's edges for one bounded rebuild-to-rebuild window, `fsck`-visible as `unaccounted` — preferred to violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY`.

topic: GC safety is independent of the
canonical_claim: GC safety is independent of the advisory heartbeat; the heartbeat is the minimal addition needed to prevent a slow leader's frozen round sequence from triggering a false steal.

topic: The root local model shows that
canonical_claim: The root-local model shows that a target-sharded fold needs one global coordinator fence and paired old-binding `−1` deltas; per-reducer fencing or inferring the old target from the new ref is unsafe.

topic: The E3 GC redesign used root
canonical_claim: The E3 GC redesign used root-local part manifests and source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, removed the registry, and added a shard-incarnation ABA guard.

topic: The E4 GC and writer settlement
canonical_claim: The E4 GC and writer settlement uses a one-pass heartbeat ack-floor round, writer point-reads of freshness metadata instead of a `RetireView`, retired rows inside the snapshot run, and a ref snapshot plus append log instead of a mutable root-shard manifest.

topic: retired sentinel rows
canonical_claim: Retired rows are represented as `kCondemned` sentinel rows inside the snapshot run rather than as a separate retired-list object. Retired entries can ride the source-edge snapshot as condemned-sentinel rows, reducing the GC merge from three cursors to two; a separate incremental LSM snapshot is an independent later optimization.

topic: The GC side ack floor one
canonical_claim: The GC-side ack-floor one-pass round is current, while the writer-side ack-floor and `RetireView` synchronization was deleted by `55b76af5998`; these are separate mechanisms.

topic: one-pass ack-floor GC round
canonical_claim: The regular GC round is one pass consisting of a heartbeat ack floor, one `LIST` discovery sweep, a three-cursor fold, pre-CAS deletes, and one `gc/state` CAS. The ack-floor GC redesign replaces O(universe) per-round fence and recheck phases with a merged per-server heartbeat, a current retired list, and a one-pass three-cursor merge. The planned one-pass ack-floor round computes the heartbeat floor before discovery, folds and merges deltas, deletes graduated entries by exact token, writes retired-list objects, and then performs one `gc/state` CAS; `fence` and `recheck` are removed. The ack-floor GC round replaces fence and recheck phases with a three-cursor streaming merge and one `gc/state` CAS; graduation requires `condemn_round < min_ack` and two-phase `delete_pending` handling. The current GC implementation (Gc class, CasGc.h) is a leader-paced ack-floor redesign (spec 2026-07-02): one pass per round consisting of a heartbeat ack floor over MountLease.observed_gc_round, a three-cursor merge fold, two-phase condemn/graduation deletion, and a single gc/state CAS; the older fence_round/recheck terminology survives only as fossil comments/variable names.

topic: The GC lease is work de
canonical_claim: The GC lease is work de-duplication rather than mutual exclusion: one `gc/state` CAS adopts a round, attempt-scoped artifacts isolate leaders, pre-CAS destructive work uses published state, and exact-token deletes protect newer incarnations.

topic: The D1 implementation plan replaces gc
canonical_claim: The D1 implementation plan replaces `gc/registry` discovery with `LIST(cas/refs/)` and reclaims empty ref-shard objects so `dropNamespace` no longer leaks a monotone registry and empty shard objects.

topic: The D1 design collapses the prior
canonical_claim: The D1 design collapses the prior fence coordinates into two orthogonal coordinates: immutable shard `incarnation` for identity and birth ordering, plus pool-global GC `round` for the writer retire-view floor.

topic: D1 makes LIST cas refs the
canonical_claim: D1 makes `LIST(cas/refs/)` the discovery authority, retains ambiguity detection across pages as a fail-closed condition, and removes `gc/registry`, `RootsRegistry`, `rootsRegistryKey`, `ensureRegistered`, the registry-fence sub-step, and the `_registry` cursor branch.

topic: dropNamespace appends an explicit tombstone as
canonical_claim: `dropNamespace` appends an explicit tombstone as the last journal event after ref removals, and GC deletes the shard only when it is empty, tombstoned, and folded past a completed fence using `deleteExact(rootShardKey(ns, shard), token)`.

topic: After registry removal GC fences only
canonical_claim: After registry removal, GC fences only discovered shards from `LIST(cas/refs/)`; an absent shard is not minted or fenced, and create ordering is supplied by the precommit gate.

topic: The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC
canonical_claim: The consolidation target explicitly assigns GC protocol documentation to cover lease/election, rounds, orphan and ref removal, shard reclaim, incarnation, registry removal, attempt-scoped generations, TLA+ references, and S3 budget links.

topic: The current retired list design adds
canonical_claim: The current retired-list design adds `RetiredEntry::condemn_round`, adds `GcState::retired_refs`, uses `cas_gc_state` version 4, rejects v3 fail-closed, and has `RetireView::refresh` GET `gc/state` followed by each referenced retired-list object without LIST.

topic: The redesigned regular GC round targets
canonical_claim: The redesigned regular GC round targets O(delta) plus O(servers) S3 requests; its only universe-proportional operation is the existing LIST sweep, which costs O(universe/1000) LIST requests.

topic: The retired list is one current
canonical_claim: The retired list is one current sorted candidate set referenced by `gc/state.retired_refs`; per-round retired sets keyed by `retiredKey(...)` and the multi-round `RetireView` fetch protocol are removed.

topic: gc state removes fence_version adds current
canonical_claim: `gc/state` removes `fence_version`, adds current retired-list references and checksums, and is updated with one CAS per pass containing the round, generation adoption, retired references, and coverage.

topic: fence_round is no longer bumped every
canonical_claim: `fence_round` is no longer bumped every round; it remains only as the birth floor stamped at root-shard creation for THM-NO-RETURN newborn ordering.

topic: Graduation is two phase a pass
canonical_claim: Graduation is two-phase: a pass marks fresh graduates with `delete_pending = true` and keeps them published, while `deleteExact` runs only for entries already pending in the previous published list.

topic: Snapshot run streaming scope includes T2
canonical_claim: Snapshot-run streaming scope includes T2 streaming reads and T0 reference-parent runs for empty-delta shards; T1 delta-runs are deferred to a subsequent specification.

topic: The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration
canonical_claim: The rebuild plan uses attempt iteration over batches of at most `rebuild_edge_budget` edges, feeding the previous attempt's runs back as `prior_runs`; this provides O(budget) memory without new spill/merge classes.

topic: GC trim uses mutateShard as a
canonical_claim: GC trim uses `mutateShard` as a `WholeShard` queue item, so trim rewrites no longer race writers even though trim still flushes alone.

topic: GC Lever A skips the expensive
canonical_claim: GC Lever A skips the expensive in-degree snapshot rebuild on rounds with no destructive decision; Lever B, an incremental point-updatable in-degree store, remains out of scope.

topic: Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for
canonical_claim: Using a stale heartbeat acknowledgement for a renewal is conservative for the GC floor because it can only lower `min_ack` and delay graduation; lease expiry is the failure that must be avoided.

topic: The phase 4 GC optimization skips
canonical_claim: The phase-4 GC optimization skips unchanged namespaces so an idle round approaches O(servers) reads and a small-delta round costs O(delta), with a mandatory TLA+ proof that owner-removal events are never skipped.

topic: The dangling precommit fix uses a
canonical_claim: The dangling-precommit fix uses a fold-side, watermark-keyed force-Read: `ShardCoverage` records the minimal live precommit binding, and `computeDiscoverDecisions` overrides `Skip` when that precommit is provably dead.

topic: Build abandon retires build_seq after its
canonical_claim: Build::abandon retires build_seq after its precommit-removal CAS, while alive is set false early.

topic: Graduation is re keyed from condemn_round
canonical_claim: Graduation is re-keyed from condemn_round < min_ack to condemn_round < current_round, with min_ack removed from the GC fold interface.

topic: After v3 the retired list is
canonical_claim: After v3, the retired list is GC-private: writers make condemned decisions through per-hash `.meta` point reads and do not read `RetiredSet`.

topic: Retired in snapshot preserves settlement semantics
canonical_claim: Retired-in-snapshot preserves settlement semantics including condemn, carry, round-paced graduation, `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, the pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters.

topic: The two cursor merge settles a
canonical_claim: The two-cursor merge settles a pending row by exact-token redelete at d = 0, spares any row at d > 0, graduates a nonpending row when `condemn_round < current_round`, and otherwise carries it unchanged.

topic: In place journal trimming was replaced
canonical_claim: In-place journal trimming was replaced by cleanup of `_log` and superseded `_snap` objects only when both durable cursor coverage and observed snapshot coverage exist.

topic: CAS listing and exact delete handling
canonical_claim: CAS listing and exact-delete handling is intended to share a callback-based `forEachListedKey` iterator and a `classifyDeleteOutcome` classifier across GC, fsck, and orphan-manifest cleanup.

topic: GcState fence_seq is write only vestigial
canonical_claim: `GcState::fence_seq` is write-only vestigial state because GC outcome and retire keys use `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`; its proto field is removed and field number 3/name `fence_seq` are reserved.

topic: ShardCoverage folded_cursor and ShardCoverage incarnation have
canonical_claim: `ShardCoverage::folded_cursor` and `ShardCoverage::incarnation` have no production readers and are removed from the fold-seal format while the `ShardIncarnation` type itself is retained.

topic: GC fold body reads should size
canonical_claim: GC fold body reads should size each fresh `ReadBufferFromS3` from the known listed/meta body size plus small slack, capped at the current default; the expected effect is approximately 99% less fold-buffer churn with no behavior change.

topic: Manifest debris must be drained before
canonical_claim: Manifest debris must be drained before deleting the victim mount slot because deleting the mount body removes `floorForNamespace` watermark authority and would make the debris ineligible forever; the decommission command is the epoch authority and can sweep old-epoch prefixes.

topic: The rev 6 GC defense audit
canonical_claim: The rev.6 GC-defense audit treats zero S3 requests spent fighting a foreign writer on hot paths as the compliance principle; incidental checks and CAS-linearized commits are compliant by definition.

topic: A new GC leader starts lease
canonical_claim: A new GC leader starts lease observation afresh, delaying fencing by one round without weakening safety because fencing is a liveness and cleanup mechanism.

topic: The rev 6 GC defense audit

topic: A proposed manifest cache is keyed

The useful manifest-body cache scope is one GC round: an op-scoped or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid cross-transaction re-reads; the HEAD-before-GET pair remains vetoed from change. In the measured intake, 7,565 edge reads were re-reads across 4,573 distinct manifests, or 39.6%; all observed re-reads were cross-transaction and none were intra-transaction. In that fold window, 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, and `CasManifestGet == CasRefEmittedEdges`, demonstrating that no manifest-body cache existed. 39.6% of GC intake manifest fetches are re-reads (7,565 edges over 4,573 distinct manifests): intra-transaction redundancy is exactly zero, and all of it is cross-transaction (2,991 manifests carry both an add and a remove edge in the window, so the same body is read once when the ref is published and again when it is dropped), making a round-scoped body cache — not an op- or transaction-scoped one — the effective lever.

topic: cas gc rebuild s security verdict

topic: republishRef can reach the overwrite leak when a

topic: The all-tree part-files design stores txn_version.txt, metadata_version.txt, and

topic: A precommit may name only a manifest minted

topic: The new ShardCoverage fields are has_live_precommit, min_live_precommit_writer_epoch, and

topic: Decoded PartManifest::entries must be strictly ascending by path

topic: A same-manifest re-promote is allowed and must be

topic: A committed CAS repoint is implemented as the
canonical_claim: A committed CAS repoint is implemented as the existing `publishEntries` sequence plus an `allow_repoint` mode on `Build::promote`, matching the modeled TLA transition `WRepoint`. For a ref key `K`, `repointRef` maps to `WRepoint(mOld, mNew, ref=K, w)`: one journal event in one namespace carries `old=Bind(mOld)` and `new=Bind(mNew)` under the same ref. `Build::promote` accepts a trailing `bool allow_repoint = false`; when it is true and the committed ref names a different manifest, it emits one committed-transition RefOp from the current `ManifestRef` to the new `id.ref` and emits `CasEventType::RefRepoint`. `repointRef(const PartRefKey &, std::vector<Cas::ManifestEntry>, Cas::ProvenanceOp)` returns false and performs zero pool mutations or events when the candidate manifest is byte-equal to the committed manifest; otherwise it publishes with `allow_repoint=true`, increments `ProfileEvents::CasRefRepoint`, logs the ref and entry count at warning level, and erases the cached folder view on success.

topic: Pool/CasRefLedger owns ref-table state and locks, ref transaction

topic: RefCowMap consists of an immutable shared std::shared_ptr<const std::map<String
canonical_claim: `RefCowMap` consists of an immutable shared `std::shared_ptr<const std::map<String, RefCommittedRow>> base` and a per-copy `std::map<String, std::optional<RefCommittedRow>> overlay`, with present entries as overrides and `nullopt` as tombstones. `RefCowMap` copies share the immutable base and copy only the overlay, keyed reads check overlay before base, point writes modify overlay, ordered iteration merges both sorted ranges, and `materialize()` folds the overlay into a fresh base once per flush. `RefCowMap::materialize()` merges overlay values and tombstones into a new immutable base, then clears the overlay and resets `net_delta`. `RefCowMap` keyed access checks overlay entries first, treats tombstones as misses, writes only to overlay, and performs sorted two-range merge iteration for cold full scans. `RefCowMap::materialize()` is O(n) once per flush and restores `base + empty overlay`, so ordinary keyed reads between flushes access the base without merge overhead.

topic: Before the incremental-budget change, admits() fully rebuilt and
canonical_claim: Before the incremental-budget change, `admits()` fully rebuilt and encoded both a snapshot and a hypothetical whole-namespace removal transaction for every state-growing operation, making a K-op batch against N live refs cost O(K×N). The new `admits()` applies the candidate operation to a scratch state and compares `snapshotFramingSize + snapshot_body_bytes` and `removalFramingSize + removal_body_bytes` against the budgets, reducing a flush batch from O(K×N) to O(K) while preserving the existing preview identifiers and framing. The incremental `admits()` plan replaces the O(N)-per-operation full re-encode with two running body-byte totals on `RefTableState`, turning a K-op flush batch against an N-ref table from O(K×N) into O(K) with byte-identical decisions.

topic: The only row-population paths for RefTableState are stateFromSnapshot
canonical_claim: The only row-population paths for `RefTableState` are `stateFromSnapshot` and `applyOpInPlace`; these are therefore the only paths that seed or maintain the body-byte counters. The incremental-budget implementation maintains `snapshot_body_bytes` and `removal_body_bytes` at five row-mutation sites in `applyOpInPlace` and seeds them once in `stateFromSnapshot`.

topic: The size helpers committedRowEncodedSize, precommitRowEncodedSize, snapshotFramingSize, re
canonical_claim: The size helpers `committedRowEncodedSize`, `precommitRowEncodedSize`, `snapshotFramingSize`, `removalOpEncodedSize`, and `removalFramingSize` calculate sizes by using the same encoder fragments as the full formats, avoiding hand-written escaping or length arithmetic. The incremental-budget size helpers are factored from the existing snapshot and log encoders so per-row and framing sizes remain byte-identical to full encoding by construction.

topic: The incremental admits() change does not alter the
canonical_claim: The incremental `admits()` change does not alter the ref wire format or persisted data and needs no compatibility scaffolding because CAS is pre-release. topic: CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered retries the whole recovery attempt, including namesp
canonical_claim: `CasRefLedger::ensureRefTableRecovered` retries the whole recovery attempt, including namespace `LIST`, snapshot/log `GET`s, replay, and the seal `PUT`, rather than retrying only the seal. Each CAS ref-table recovery retry starts from a fresh `LIST`, and the recovery steps are idempotent because the seal uses a conditional `PUT` with a deterministic `seal_id` and resolves an already-landed identical seal as `Committed`.

topic: RefCowMap::find creates a non-mergeable base iterator for an
canonical_claim: `RefCowMap::find` creates a non-mergeable base iterator for an overlay-only key, so incrementing the iterator can skip later base entries even though the primitive is documented as a `std::map` replacement. `RefCowMap::find` builds a non-mergeable iterator for overlay-only keys by using `base->find(key)` instead of the sibling base branch's `lower_bound`; with base={A,D} and overlay-only B, `find("B")` then `++` hits a state bitwise equal to `end()` and silently skips D. Not reachable through current point-dereference-only callers, but the fix (`lower_bound`) is a strict improvement, identical when the key is shadowed.

topic: After encapsulation, RefTableState keeps lifecycle, transaction, committed-map, precommit
canonical_claim: After encapsulation, `RefTableState` keeps lifecycle, transaction, committed-map, precommit, and byte-counter storage private; external code reads through accessors and mutates state only through protocol entry points such as `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `admits`. `RefTableState` was encapsulated as a closed class with private fields and public getters; mutation is restricted to `applyRefLogTxn`, `replay`, `stateFromSnapshot`, and `materializeCommitted`.

topic: Recovery replay streams post-snapshot RefLogTxn objects one at
canonical_claim: Recovery replay streams post-snapshot `RefLogTxn` objects one at a time after sorting keys by transaction ID, reducing recovery memory to O(one transaction) regardless of tail length. Streaming ref recovery applies decoded transactions one at a time into a private candidate `RefTableState` and never mutates live `rt.state` until complete recovery is ready. The stage-1 `RefReplayBuilder` owns a private candidate, applies decoded transactions in place, discards it on failure, and returns a complete `RecoveryResult`; vanished objects re-list, while decode or apply corruption fails fast.

topic: An item with more than ref_txn_max_ops operations fails
canonical_claim: An item with more than `ref_txn_max_ops` operations fails alone, while removal-class items are exempt from the op cap only when their built operations contain `RemoveNamespace`; `WholeShard` scope alone is not the discriminator. topic: Ref transaction identifiers are allowed to have safe
canonical_claim: Ref transaction identifiers are allowed to have safe gaps: an append refused before any network attempt can leave a gap, so a missing id in an otherwise ordered sequence is not by itself evidence of incomplete enumeration. A missing sequence id is not itself anomalous because a pre-attempt refused append can leave a safe gap; an object that exists at or below the cursor but was never applied is the unambiguous anomaly.

topic: Within each (namespace, epoch), durable ref ids are
canonical_claim: Within each `(namespace, epoch)`, durable ref ids are dense from 1 through the greatest applied sequence, and the next id is `greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1`; the pool-wide `next_ref_sequence` allocator is removed. `CasRefLedger::allocateRefTxnId` derives ids per namespace from `getGreatestApplied()`: `{E, greatest_applied.ref_sequence + 1}` in the same epoch, or `{E, 1}` after an epoch change; `next_ref_sequence` is deleted.

topic: After any writer-epoch transition, the first touch CAS-walks
canonical_claim: After any writer-epoch transition, the first touch CAS-walks the dead tail using the `slot-occupy` result states `Created`, `Occupied(bytes, token)`, and `Unresolved`; an occupied `EpochSeal` terminates the walk, while an occupied straggler is adopted and replayed. During recovery epoch transitions, `Created` closes an epoch, an occupied seal is adopted, an occupied non-seal straggler at `T+1` is applied and the seal is retried at the new `T+1`, and `Unresolved` enters transient retry; recovery never mints `T+2` blindly. The first recovery or touch after every writer-epoch transition, including a clean transition, must CAS-walk and seal the previous nonempty stream; an adopted EpochSeal terminates the walk.

topic: Checkpoint updates use one read-validate-merge-token-CAS algorithm for append
canonical_claim: Checkpoint updates use one read-validate-merge-token-CAS algorithm for append, snapshot publication, and sealing; identical merged bodies skip the CAS, and a contribution above `committed_through` is corruption. `publishCkpt` follows read, validate, merge, identical-body skip, and token-CAS; token conflicts retry only until the deadline, and every attempt reruns `checkFenceOrThrow(admitted_generation)` after its read and before its CAS. If merging proposed _ckpt fields produces the exact current body, the publisher must return without a same-bytes CAS; recovery or merge retries must use the existing recovery deadline and bounded-restart accounting.

topic: The append order is immutable log PUT, _ckpt.committed_through
canonical_claim: The append order is immutable log PUT, `_ckpt.committed_through` CAS, in-memory install/acknowledge, and allocation of the next id; if the frontier publication is unresolved, the lane remains `NeedsRecovery` and returns no success. The ref durability order is `log PUT → _ckpt CAS → ack`, and retry-after-conflict must perform a whole-body exact re-read and re-merge regardless of the first-attempt `_ckpt` view policy.

topic: The prev_epoch_seal field is populated by recovery seals
canonical_claim: The `prev_epoch_seal` field is populated by recovery seals and by every ordinary sequence-1 transaction after an epoch transition; recovery installs the chain's final seal in `RefTableRuntime::last_epoch_seal`. A namespace's genesis epoch is its life_epoch; last_epoch_seal is none exactly at genesis, and sequence 1 requires prev_epoch_seal iff writer_epoch > life_epoch

For incarnation-keyed `_ckpt`, joining an unknown `life_epoch` with `E` yields `E`, joining `E` with `E` yields `E`, and two different present `life_epoch` values in one incarnation are corruption rather than `max`; `checkpoint_snapshot_id` and `last_epoch_seal` still merge by semantic maximum.

topic: tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce must make the immutable snapshot body durable
canonical_claim: `tryPublishSnapshotAndAdvanceCheckpointOnce` must make the immutable snapshot body durable, advance `_ckpt`, and only then adopt the snapshot in memory; retry and backoff semantics remain unchanged. The three publication effects are ordered as durable snapshot body, advanced `_ckpt`, and in-memory adoption; `Poisoned` refuses publication and triggers re-recovery. CasRefLedger::trySnapshotPublishOnce must publish _ckpt after the snapshot body is durable and test its race, identical-body no-op, token conflict, and fence behavior through the real call site A normal snapshot publication writes the snapshot body before advancing the publisher checkpoint, and the body PUT and checkpoint CAS are each observed as one request for the publication attempt. Snapshot publication records the _snap body with ref_request_controller->putIfAbsentControlled(refSnapshotKey(...)) before calling publishCkptContribution(...); reversing that order makes the ordering test fail.

topic: A permanent Retired catalog history grows with every
canonical_claim: A permanent `Retired` catalog history grows with every historical namespace and eventually makes legitimate admissions return `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; normal `Atomic` UUID churn does not bound that history. An immortal `Retired` row makes the catalog `O(historical namespaces)` on the hot full-object CAS path and eventually exhausts the catalog's admission budget; exact compaction is unavailable for arbitrary opaque names.

topic: Before its fix, Build::promote could overwrite an existing
canonical_claim: Before its fix, `Build::promote` could overwrite an existing committed `refs[R]` without emitting a removal for the old binding, leaving two committed owner bindings for `R` and permanently pinning the old manifest and uniquely-owned blobs. `Build::promote` overwrites `refs[R]` without emitting a committed-to-committed repoint event, so the previously committed manifest and its uniquely owned blobs remain pinned forever. `Build::promote` can overwrite an existing committed ref (`refs[dst]=T_a`) with a new manifest (`T_b`) without releasing `T_a`, permanently orphaning (leaking) the old manifest and its blobs; this is the most concrete confirmed storage leak from the review. Fix: `Build::promote` must, when `refs[R]` already names another manifest, either emit a proper committed-to-committed repoint or fail closed with an exception; also move `Build::abandon`'s `retireBuildSeq` call after the removal mutation.

topic: Treating a vanished catalog as an empty catalog
canonical_claim: Treating a vanished catalog as an empty catalog is unsafe: the retry path could replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` is the fail-closed analogue. A retry path that treats a vanished CAS catalog object as an empty catalog is a silent-default-substitution defect: on retry after a vanish, it would replace every namespace's catalog with a single mutation's output via create-if-absent; the in-tree analogue `PoolMeta::admitOrValidate` already fails closed on exactly that observation and was cited as the pattern to follow.

topic: Any operation that changes committed root.refs or committed
canonical_claim: Any operation that changes committed `root.refs` or committed `RootRef::mutable_files` must be a method on `CachedPartFolderAccess`. `ContentAddressedTransaction` committed part-reference mutations must replace raw `Store::dropRef`, raw `Store::updateRefPublishedAt`, direct final `Build::promote`, and table/shadow namespace drops with facade calls.

canonical_claim: Snapshot publication must re-evaluate the accumulated tail or remember and re-fire a pending trigger, because single-flight suppression can otherwise let a publication of chunk 1 hide chunks 2 through N indefinitely.

topic: A ref-log transaction can become durable before its

topic: The residual Late-Predecessor-PUT ref-loss race is mitigated only
canonical_claim: The residual Late-Predecessor-PUT ref-loss race is mitigated only by the snapshot_min_log_age_ms grace window (a candidate ref snapshot never covers a tail region younger than this age); ProfileEvents::CasRefLatePredecessorObserved increments once per trySnapshotPublishOnce call in which that grace window forces an early break, making the residual race measurable rather than only mitigated.

topic: Every cross-thread copy of a live RefTableState must
canonical_claim: Every cross-thread copy of a live `RefTableState` must be created AND destroyed under `state_mutex`, so that a `use_count()` of 1 observed under that lock is stable against both increment and decrement; this invariant is documented in both COW headers (`RefCowMap`, `RefCowManifestSet`).

topic: The in-place fold's coherence ordering: per overlay entry
canonical_claim: The in-place fold's coherence ordering: per overlay entry, the base mutation (its only throw point) runs first, then the non-throwing `net_delta` adjust and `overlay.erase`; at every escape point `(base, overlay, net_delta)` stays exactly coherent, load-bearing because materialize runs after a durable PUT and a tracked-allocator OOM must not corrupt live bookkeeping.

topic: In-place trusted-replay apply is safe because every production
canonical_claim: In-place trusted-replay apply is safe because every production call site of `admits`/`applyRefLogTxn`/`replay` runs either under the ledger's `state_mutex` or on a detached/local copy, so no concurrent reader can observe a state mid-mutation; COW writes touch only the per-copy overlay, never the shared immutable base.

topic: The recovery-latency fix (G) materializes only the one
canonical_claim: The recovery-latency fix (G) materializes only the one retained recovery-adopt site (`CasRefLedger.cpp:426`) before retaining its replayed state; the fsck/GC `replay`/`recoverRefTable` locals (`CasFsck.cpp`, `CasOrphanManifestSweep.cpp`, `CasGc.cpp`) are iterated once and dropped, so they are deliberately left unmaterialized.

topic: The flat-combining shard-mutation queue (Store::mutateShard) serializes intra-server write
canonical_claim: The flat-combining shard-mutation queue (`Store::mutateShard`) serializes intra-server writers per `(namespace, shard)`: the caller finding the queue leaderless flushes batches (one read, apply-all in order with per-closure snapshot isolation, one `casPut`) until its own item completes; the carve runs after the flush's first read so S3 read latency IS the batching window, turning the old positive-feedback conflict loop under load into a negative one. At most one mutation per ref name is allowed per flush; `WholeShard` closures (trim, fence, dropNamespace, reclaim) and create-if-absent flushes run solo.

topic: The ref-lane flush uses a per-table "wedge": at
canonical_claim: The ref-lane flush uses a per-table "wedge": at most one outstanding record per table holding the key and sealed bytes of a single conditional PUT whose outcome is unresolved. The next flush must resolve that exact key (via `resolveByExactGet`) before it may allocate a new transaction id, which is what realizes INV-14 (fail-closed on ambiguity) and prevents the ledger from ever silently creating a gap or double-publishing.

topic: RefTableState holds a copy-on-write map of committed rows
canonical_claim: `RefTableState` holds a copy-on-write map of committed rows, a set of precommits, an O(1) manifest-ownership index enforcing the one-owner-per-manifest invariant, a lifecycle (`Live`/`Removed`), the greatest applied transaction id, and O(1)-maintained body-size counters for admission. Two mutexes have a fixed lock order `ref_queue_mutex -> state_mutex`, never the reverse, and network I/O is never performed under `state_mutex`, so a reader sees either a whole transaction or none of it.

topic: Recovery of a ref table on first touch
canonical_claim: Recovery of a ref table on first touch performs a paginated LIST of `cas/ns/stream/<life-id>/`, takes the greatest snapshot, replays every log strictly greater than it one transaction at a time, restarts on a vanished object (bounded at 3 attempts, treated as concurrent GC cleanup rather than corruption), and on an unclean boundary publishes a recovery seal snapshot at the synthetic id `{my_epoch - 1, UINT64_MAX}` before exposing the table, so that id dominates any straggler the dead epoch could still materialize.

topic: Under CAS's RefLaneState model, relink certification is Ready-state-only
canonical_claim: Under CAS's `RefLaneState` model, relink certification is Ready-state-only: a resumed relink gate consumes a single-state precondition instead of the twelve-row cross-product the earlier encoding required, and the NETWORK_ERROR/terminal split means only `Closed`/`Faulted` are non-retriable while all other states retry.

topic: The ref state machine's load-bearing invariant is that
canonical_claim: The ref state machine's load-bearing invariant is that `promote` never silently displaces a different committed row for the same name; a silent displacement would never emit the evicted manifest's -1 edge, leaking it phantom-alive forever. `stateFromSnapshot` round-trips a hand-built snapshot through the codec so the same bug class cannot enter via snapshot loading.

topic: cleanupRefObjects only deletes ref logs/snapshots that are covered
canonical_claim: `cleanupRefObjects` only deletes ref logs/snapshots that are covered by BOTH the durable fold cursor AND a durable snapshot; GC never invents a ref transition, and dead-precommit cleanup (appending exact owner_transition removals) is the writer's job, not GC's.

topic: Ref transaction IDs (RefTxnId = {writer_epoch, ref_sequence}) are
canonical_claim: Ref transaction IDs (`RefTxnId = {writer_epoch, ref_sequence}`) are strictly increasing with epoch as the primary component, so a recreated namespace always gets greater ids than a prior life — no ABA check is needed on ref-log ordering.

canonical_claim: Loose mountpoint files are not namespaces — they are path-owned plain objects with conditional overwrite/exact deletion, drained by server-root decommission. topic: A CAS container recreated without persistent /var/lib/clickhouse gets a

topic: Rapid repeated crash-restart in S13 could wedge mount-lease self-adoption
canonical_claim: Rapid repeated crash-restart in S13 could wedge mount-lease self-adoption with `key '...ca_soak_ch1/mount' was touched while adopting our own mount slot`; the node stayed down with exit code 49 until the mount object was manually deleted. The original P1 availability bug was a cold-open adoption race in which GC fencing landed between the non-atomic GET and PUT in `Store::open`, causing exit 49 with `touched while adopting our own mount slot`. The cold-open path has no retry around the GET→PUT adoption window, so a fence landing there throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` `touched while adopting our own mount slot` during metadata load and leaves the container down with exit 49. A CA mount could wedge after rapid crash-restart because a GC leader legitimately fenced an expired lease while the renewal thread was blocked by synchronous `refreshViewForBeat` S3 reads, and the non-atomic self-adopt GET-to-CAS window had no retry.

topic: MountLeaseKeeper renewal can block beyond the 30-second TTL because
canonical_claim: `MountLeaseKeeper` renewal can block beyond the 30-second TTL because `prepareRenew` runs `Store::refreshViewForBeat`, which may wait for exclusive `view_gate` access and perform retired-view S3 reads. The old renewal path could let a slow retired-view refresh or `view_gate` drain delay the lease PUT beyond the 30-second TTL during RustFS retry storms, causing GC to fence a fully alive server; the observed RustFS read-error rate was about 19%.

topic: P1 was a chronic mount-lease race with about 26

topic: During Store teardown, a lease-renewal on_lost callback can re-arm
canonical_claim: During `Store` teardown, a lease-renewal `on_lost` callback can re-arm `remount_thread` after its only join because `scheduleRemount` does not guard shutdown, causing an unjoined `ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl` to terminate the process. Store::~Store() can abort() the process: a lease-renewal failure during teardown re-arms remount_thread after the destructor's only join, because scheduleRemount() gates only on config.background_watermark and remount_running (never on a shutdown flag), so a fresh ThreadFromGlobalPool gets move-assigned into remount_thread after the join already passed; both ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl::operator=(&&) and its destructor call abort() on a still-initialized target, so member destruction aborts. This is a guaranteed process crash under a realistic interleaving (an ordinary fenced-out or transiently-failing mount lease during DROP/disk-detach/server-shutdown), and was rated a blocker (risk 90) in the umbrella review of cas-gc-rebuild.

topic: The four B3 health columns are currently stamped identically

topic: A sustained object-store fault can fail the mount-lease renewal

topic: SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop treats any exception from renewOnce as terminal, while
canonical_claim: `SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` treats any exception from `renewOnce` as terminal, while `renewOnce` can throw from `putOverwrite` before checking the returned token; a transient network fault is therefore misread as foreign-token supersession and burns the writer incarnation. The CI reproducer for the mount-lease self-race is a `putOverwrite` that applies to backend state and then throws a transient exception, followed by a confirmed mismatch against the stale token; the background loop must fence and invoke `on_lost` without process death. `SingleWriterSlot::backgroundLoop` continues after transient renewal failures while the confirmed lease deadline remains safe, but a definite `PreconditionFailed` mismatch always stops the loop and routes to `onRenewFailed` and self-remount recovery.

topic: Review finding №9 is real: decommission can delete a
canonical_claim: Review finding №9 is real: decommission can delete a successor's fresh mount and epoch objects after releasing the impersonated lease, violating durable epoch monotonicity. Decommissioning can delete a successor mount's control objects because it releases the administrative claim before rereading and deleting current epoch, owner, and mount objects. Decommission must inspect every `DeleteOutcome`, abort the tail on any non-`Deleted` result, and delete mount before the claimed epoch and owner so successor objects cannot be reclaimed. The decommission tail must delete the farewell mount token first, then the epoch token captured under the claim, and owner last; every non-`Deleted` result aborts the tail and retains the slot.

topic: A mount-lease renewal mismatch under the keeper's own (uuid
canonical_claim: A mount-lease renewal mismatch under the keeper's own `(uuid, epoch)` can construct `LOGICAL_ERROR` and abort ASan or debug builds; the intended response is fail-closed uncertainty with a fence and self-remount. For a same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced mount body, `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` with state-uncertainty diagnostics and relies on fencing plus self-remount rather than constructing `LOGICAL_ERROR`. For a same-uuid body with a different writer epoch, `onRenewMismatch` throws `ABORTED` as the normal superseded fencing outcome and reports `superseded by a newer incarnation`. The former `MountLeaseKeeper::onRenewMismatch` classifier handled GC-fenced same-uuid bodies, different-uuid bodies, and vanished bodies but had no branch for same-uuid, same-epoch, unfenced bodies. An earlier renewal PUT can land while its client-side timeout loses the acknowledgement, bumping the mount token or sequence; the next retry then presents a stale token and reaches the classifier gap even though the body looks self-owned. Phase A classifies same-uuid/same-epoch/unfenced as `same_epoch_state_uncertain` with `ABORTED`, same-uuid/different-epoch as `superseded` with `ABORTED`, foreign uuid as `LOGICAL_ERROR`, and absent body as `FILE_DOESNT_EXIST`.

topic: The v9 recovery and wedge paths must recheck the
canonical_claim: The v9 recovery and wedge paths must recheck the captured mount-fence generation immediately before every mutation: `slot-occupy`, `_ckpt` publication, install, unwedge, or equivalent retry publication. The v9 mount recovery layer captures `(actor, generation, op)` identity at admission and rechecks generation after I/O before every publication; an `Occupied` `slot-occupy` result must be resolved by comparing bytes. The proven three same-value sites are slot-occupy, _ckpt CAS, and recovery install sharing one captured generation; the catalog token is a distinct ZombieGoLive credential Recovery must capture the mount fence generation at admission and require the same generation plus a non-superseded runtime for every slot-occupy, _ckpt CAS, and final install; remount must cancel or wait for recovery before rearming. Recovery installation and wedge retries are guarded by the fence generation captured at recovery start; a successor seal conclusively rejects an old-generation retry.

topic: Proposed fix for the Store::~Store() teardown abort: add a

topic: rebuildBaseline (cas-gc-rebuild) has no mount-lease interlock: a live server's

Confirmed as a real bug by the feature owner ("Yep, this looks real... gc-rebuild i've added recently, and it almost untested"). A regression test `CasGcRebuild.GCR1_NoMountLeaseInterlock_RunsUnderLiveMount` demonstrates rebuild running under a live mount; the fix flips the assertion to `EXPECT_FALSE(rep.performed)` with a mount-related refusal string.

topic: SEC-7: the write/GC audit's fencing findings (J1/J2/J3) are attacker-amplifiable
canonical_claim: SEC-7: the write/GC audit's fencing findings (J1/J2/J3) are attacker-amplifiable — an attacker who can skew a victim's clock via unauthenticated NTP can force a premature mount-lease reclaim and induce split-brain (J3), and an attacker who can induce a long stop-the-world pause (resource exhaustion, cgroup throttling) widens the unfenced `mayMutate()` to `casPut` window for a zombie write (J1); TLS protects S3 transit but NTP is typically unauthenticated. Recommendation: carry `writer_epoch` into the shard-CAS precondition, and require authenticated time (NTS/authenticated NTP) in deployment guidance.
